title: Tripartite Entanglement in $e^+ e^- \to t \bar{t} Z$
summary: Multipartite entanglement is a uniquely quantum form of correlation that captures collective properties of a composite quantum state beyond those encoded in its bipartite subsystems. We investigate this phenomenon in the process $e^+e^-\to t\bar tZ$ at a future lepton collider, where the final state spins span the tripartite Hilbert space $\mathscr{H}=\mathbb{C}^{2}\otimes\mathbb{C}^{2}\otimes\mathbb{C}^{3}$. Starting from the Standard Model helicity amplitudes, we reconstruct the full $12\times 12$ spin density matrix and characterise its entanglement structure through one-to-one negativities, one-to-other negativities, and the genuine multipartite negativity, evaluated at three increasingly inclusive levels of phase space integration. Pairwise entanglement is generally suppressed relative to the collective (one-to-other) and the genuine multipartite entanglement, and all measures decrease as more kinematic information is integrated out. Assuming quantum tomography in the fully leptonic decay channel at $\sqrt{s}=1$ TeV, we find that the collective entanglement is accessible at a realistic high-luminosity polarised lepton collider, while a direct observation of genuine multipartite entanglement is challenging and would benefit from further optimisation of the event analysis and observable choice. The study establishes $e^+e^-\to t\bar tZ$ as an attractive laboratory for probing multipartite entanglement in high-energy collisions and provides a general mixed state framework that applies to any tripartite spin system.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates multipartite entanglement in the $e^+e^- \to t\bar{t}Z$ process at a future lepton collider, reconstructing the full 12×12 spin density matrix from SM helicity amplitudes and quantifying entanglement via negativities; it finds collective (one-to-other) entanglement is most accessible experimentally, while genuine multipartite entanglement remains challenging to observe directly.
AI.motivation: To probe multipartite entanglement — a uniquely quantum, collective correlation beyond bipartite structure — in high-energy particle collisions, using $e^+e^- \to t\bar{t}Z$ as a theoretically clean and experimentally viable tripartite spin system ($\mathbb{C}^2 \otimes \mathbb{C}^2 \otimes \mathbb{C}^3$).
AI.method: Reconstructs the full $12\times12$ spin density matrix from Standard Model helicity amplitudes; computes one-to-one, one-to-other, and genuine multipartite negativities; evaluates them at three levels of phase-space integration; assesses experimental feasibility via simulated quantum tomography in the fully leptonic decay channel at $\sqrt{s}=1$ TeV with polarised beams and high luminosity.
AI.result: Pairwise (one-to-one) entanglement is suppressed relative to collective (one-to-other) and genuine multipartite entanglement; all entanglement measures decrease with increasing phase-space integration; collective entanglement is accessible with realistic quantum tomography, whereas genuine multipartite entanglement detection is statistically challenging and requires optimized observables and analysis.
AI.conclusion: The $e^+e^- \to t\bar{t}Z$ process provides a compelling high-energy platform for studying multipartite entanglement; the analysis delivers a general mixed-state framework for tripartite spin systems, bridging quantum information theory and collider phenomenology.

title: EFT for Neutrino Oscillations: Theory Developments and Application to JUNO
summary: We contribute to the systematic analysis of New Physics effects in neutrino experiments using Effective Field Theory (EFT) methods. We review and extend the quantum field-theoretical formalism for generic neutrino interactions, discussing the inclusion of matter effects and deriving the connection with the density matrix formalism. On the phenomenological side, we apply this framework for the first time to medium-baseline reactor neutrino experiments. We derive analytical expressions for the relevant oscillation observables and perform a first EFT analysis of the recent JUNO dataset, extracting bounds on the leading non-standard interaction parameters.

AI.tldr: This paper develops an Effective Field Theory (EFT) framework for analyzing New Physics in neutrino experiments, extends formalism to include matter effects and density matrix connections, and applies it to JUNO data to constrain non-standard neutrino interactions.
AI.motivation: To enable systematic, model-independent analysis of New Physics in neutrino oscillations using EFT, particularly for medium-baseline reactor experiments where matter effects and quantum decoherence may play a role.
AI.method: Extends quantum field-theoretical formalism for generic neutrino interactions; incorporates matter effects; establishes link to density matrix formalism; derives analytical oscillation observables; performs first EFT-based fit to JUNO data.
AI.result: Analytical expressions for oscillation observables in medium-baseline reactor setups; first EFT-derived constraints on leading non-standard interaction (NSI) parameters from JUNO data.
AI.conclusion: The EFT framework provides a robust, general tool for probing New Physics in neutrino experiments; its application to JUNO demonstrates feasibility and sets baseline sensitivity for NSI parameters in reactor-based medium-baseline configurations.

title: Direct Detection of Millicharged Particles from Supernovae
summary: This work proposes a new terrestrial probe for millicharged particles (mCPs) and demonstrates promising discovery prospects. mCPs can be copiously produced in core-collapse supernovae (SNe), and a fraction may escape, travel to Earth and yield distinct signals. The mCP mass induces a time-of-flight (ToF) delay relative to the SN neutrino burst, opening a clean search window after the neutrino signal has passed. We compute the mCP-induced electron-recoil signals at XENONnT, JUNO, DUNE, and Hyper-Kamiokande for benchmark SN scenarios, and find that for $\varepsilon = 10^{-9}$ and sub-MeV to MeV-scale masses, more than 10 events per year can be detected. This search can improve upon existing SN cooling bound on $\varepsilon$ by up to an order of magnitude.

AI.tldr: Proposes a novel terrestrial probe for millicharged particles (mCPs) produced in supernovae, leveraging time-of-flight delay relative to neutrinos to enable clean detection in large neutrino experiments; predicts >10 events/year for ε=10⁻⁹ and sub-MeV–MeV mCP masses, improving SN cooling bounds by up to 10×.
AI.motivation: Millicharged particles (mCPs) produced abundantly in core-collapse supernovae may escape and reach Earth, offering a detectable signal distinct from neutrinos due to their mass-induced time-of-flight delay—enabling a background-suppressed search window after the neutrino burst.
AI.method: Computes mCP-induced electron-recoil signals in XENONnT, JUNO, DUNE, and Hyper-Kamiokande for benchmark core-collapse supernova scenarios, incorporating mCP production, propagation, and detection via ionization energy deposition.
AI.result: For electric charge coupling ε = 10⁻⁹ and mCP masses in the sub-MeV to MeV range, predicted event rates exceed 10 per year across multiple detectors; sensitivity improves existing supernova cooling constraints on ε by up to one order of magnitude.
AI.conclusion: Terrestrial detectors operating in coincidence with supernova neutrino alerts provide a powerful, background-suppressed probe for millicharged particles, significantly extending current astrophysical limits and opening a new discovery channel for light dark-sector particles.

title: Radiative Neutrino Mass in a Nonholomorphic $T'$ Modular Invariant Model
summary: The \texttt{T4-2-i} topology provides a one-loop realization of Majorana neutrino mass and may be viewed as a radiative extension of the type-II seesaw, with a scalar triplet, two inert scalar doublets, and singlet fermions propagating in the loop. A central difficulty in realizing this topology lies in the simultaneous presence of tree-level type-I and type-II seesaw contributions arising from the same particle content. In addition, the stability of the dark-matter candidate typically requires the introduction of an ad hoc discrete symmetry. In this work, we revisit the \texttt{T4-2-i} topology within a non-holomorphic modular-invariant framework based on the double-cover group $T'$. The presence of both even- and odd-weight polyharmonic Maaß forms considerably enlarges the space of allowed modular structures, while the residual $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry associated with the vicinity of the fixed point $τ=i$ naturally stabilizes the lightest odd state. The modular assignments forbid the dangerous tree-level contributions, determine the flavor structure of the lepton sector, and allow both fermionic and scalar dark-matter candidates. We confront the model with neutrino-oscillation data, charged-lepton-flavor-violating bounds, electroweak precision observables, the Higgs diphoton signal strength, the observed dark-matter relic abundance, the cosmological bound on the sum of neutrino masses, and direct-detection limits.Focusing on the fermionic dark-matter candidate, in which the lightest odd state is the Majorana fermion $N_1$, we find that both normal and inverted neutrino mass orderings remain viable. In the allowed region, the relic abundance is largely controlled by coannihilation with the inert scalar partners, while the spin-independent direct-detection rate remains naturally suppressed because it arises only through a loop-generated Higgs portal.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a modular-invariant realization of the T4-2-i neutrino mass topology using the double-cover group T', eliminating dangerous tree-level seesaw contributions, naturally stabilizing dark matter via residual Z2 symmetry at τ=i, and accommodating both neutrino mass orderings with fermionic (N₁) or scalar DM candidates.
AI.motivation: To resolve two key issues in the T4-2-i topology: (i) unwanted tree-level type-I and type-II seesaw contributions from the same field content, and (ii) the need for an ad hoc discrete symmetry to stabilize dark matter.
AI.method: Constructs a non-holomorphic modular-invariant extension of the T4-2-i model based on the finite modular group T′; exploits even- and odd-weight polyharmonic Maaß forms and residual ℤ₂ symmetry near the fixed point τ = i to forbid tree-level seesaw terms, fix Yukawa structures, and ensure DM stability.
AI.result: Tree-level seesaw contributions are forbidden; lepton flavor structure is fully determined by modular weights; both fermionic (N₁ Majorana) and scalar DM candidates are viable; normal and inverted neutrino mass orderings survive all constraints—including oscillation data, LFV, EWPO, h→γγ, relic density, Σmν < 0.12 eV, and direct detection—with SI scattering suppressed by loop-induced Higgs portal.
AI.conclusion: The T′-modular T4-2-i framework successfully unifies radiative neutrino mass generation, predictive lepton flavor structure, and natural DM stability without ad hoc symmetries—demonstrating that non-holomorphic modular invariance provides a robust theoretical foundation for beyond-Standard-Model physics addressing neutrino mass and dark matter simultaneously.

title: Implementing Hamiltonian Renormalization Group Flow on Quantum Computers with VAPOR
summary: While Hamiltonian Lattice Gauge Theory is gaining traction, today's limited numerical capacity leaves simulations affected by discretization errors. This motivates the implementation of renormalization group (RG) techniques to find discretization-error-free operators. To this end, we introduce VAPOR, a variational quantum algorithm that decomposes operators into Pauli strings, identifies RG flow orbits, and determines fixed points of a naively discretized operator. We illustrate this using a toy model of a kinematic operator in a symmetry-restricted SU(2) Yang-Mills theory.

AI.tldr: Introduces VAPOR, a variational quantum algorithm to identify renormalization group fixed points of discretized operators in Hamiltonian lattice gauge theory, demonstrated on a symmetry-restricted SU(2) Yang-Mills toy model.
AI.motivation: Limited numerical capacity in current Hamiltonian lattice gauge theory simulations leads to significant discretization errors; RG techniques are needed to construct discretization-error-free operators.
AI.method: VAPOR—a variational quantum algorithm that decomposes operators into Pauli strings, identifies RG flow orbits, and locates fixed points of naively discretized operators.
AI.result: Successful demonstration of VAPOR on a kinematic operator in a symmetry-restricted SU(2) Yang-Mills toy model, showing feasibility of identifying RG fixed points for error-mitigated operators.
AI.conclusion: VAPOR provides a quantum-algorithmic pathway toward constructing continuum-limit-robust observables in lattice gauge theories via RG-informed operator renormalization.

title: Kohn-Sham models for encapsulated two-dimensional materials
summary: We study Kohn-Sham Density Functional Theory (DFT) models describing the electronic structure of two-dimensional materials placed in a three-dimensional environment, encapsulated between two parallel conducting electrodes. In this geometry, the Dirichlet boundary conditions at the electrodes screen the Coulomb interaction, which becomes effectively short-ranged, of Yukawa type. We prove that some nonlinear Kohn-Sham DFT models are well-posed in this setting, both for periodic materials (such as graphene) and for quasi-periodic materials (such as twisted bilayer graphene and other moiré materials for generic incommensurate twist angles).

AI.tldr: This paper proves the well-posedness of nonlinear Kohn-Sham DFT models for 2D materials sandwiched between conducting electrodes, where Dirichlet boundary conditions induce Yukawa-type screening of Coulomb interaction; results hold for both periodic (e.g., graphene) and quasi-periodic (e.g., twisted bilayer graphene) systems.
AI.motivation: To establish rigorous mathematical foundations for Kohn-Sham DFT applied to 2D materials in realistic electrode-encapsulated geometries, where standard long-range Coulomb interactions are modified by boundary-induced screening.
AI.method: Mathematical analysis of nonlinear Kohn-Sham equations under Dirichlet boundary conditions that enforce Yukawa-type effective screening; employs functional analytic techniques to prove existence, uniqueness, and stability of solutions for both periodic and quasi-periodic settings.
AI.result: Well-posedness—existence, uniqueness, and continuous dependence on data—is established for the considered nonlinear Kohn-Sham DFT models in the electrode-encapsulated geometry, covering periodic and generic incommensurate quasi-periodic cases.
AI.conclusion: The Dirichlet-screened Kohn-Sham DFT framework is mathematically sound for modeling electronic structure of encapsulated 2D and moiré materials, enabling reliable first-principles simulations in experimentally relevant device configurations.

title: Bouncing Geodesics, Singularities, and the Cavity Thermal Product Formula in Asymptotically Flat and de Sitter Black Holes
summary: We investigate the existence and implications of ``bouncing geodesics'' in asymptotically flat Schwarzschild and Schwarzschild--de Sitter black holes. These trajectories, which probe the high-curvature regions near the black hole singularity, correspond to specific ``bouncing singularities'' in the bulk retarded Green's function. We provide a precise description of these singularities by combining the local Hadamard form with the global propagation of singularities theorem. We then derive the critical times at which the bulk retarded correlator becomes singular, considering all possible anchorings of the bouncing geodesics, including null infinity and the cosmological horizon. Finally, for black holes enclosed in a reflecting cavity, we establish a universal connection between the locations of the bouncing singularities and the spectrum of cavity quasinormal modes (QNMs) by deriving a cavity version of the thermal product formula, analogous to the one known for anti-de Sitter black holes. This relation allows one to extract information about the black hole interior from the asymptotic QNM spectrum measured at a reflecting hypersurface, even when the cosmological constant is zero or positive. We confirm this prediction through explicit examples by computing the cavity QNMs of scalar and electromagnetic fields, as well as gravitational waves, in spacetimes with asymptotically flat and de Sitter black holes.

AI.tldr: This paper studies bouncing geodesics near black hole singularities in Schwarzschild and Schwarzschild–de Sitter spacetimes, links their associated singularities in the retarded Green's function to quasinormal modes (QNMs) in a reflecting cavity, and derives a universal thermal-product-like formula connecting interior geometry to asymptotic QNM spectra—even for Λ ≥ 0.
AI.motivation: To probe black hole interiors and high-curvature regions via boundary observables—specifically, whether QNM spectra of confined black holes encode information about interior singularities and bouncing geodesics, extending known AdS results to asymptotically flat and dS cases.
AI.method: Combines local Hadamard parametrix construction with global propagation of singularities theorem to characterize singularities in the bulk retarded Green's function; computes critical singularity times for all bouncing geodesic anchorings (including null infinity and cosmological horizon); derives a cavity-modified thermal product formula linking bouncing singularity locations to QNM frequencies; verifies analytically and numerically for scalar, electromagnetic, and gravitational perturbations.
AI.result: 1) Precise characterization of bouncing-singularity structure in the retarded Green’s function; 2) Exact critical times for singularities across all geodesic anchorings; 3) A universal cavity thermal product formula relating QNM frequencies to interior bouncing times; 4) Explicit confirmation for scalar, EM, and gravitational fields in both asymptotically flat and de Sitter black hole cavities.
AI.conclusion: The asymptotic QNM spectrum of a black hole in a reflecting cavity fully encodes geometric data of its interior—including singularity-approaching bouncing geodesics—even without AdS boundary conditions. This establishes a concrete holographic-type relation between boundary spectral data and deep interior physics for Λ ≥ 0 spacetimes.

title: A High-Precision Clock Synchronization System for the CEPC Accelerator
summary: The Circular Electron Positron Collider (CEPC) distributes a reference clock distributed to 192 control nodes along its 100~km underground tunnel. The required synchronization precision is 30~ps (standard deviation). We present an enhanced White Rabbit (WR)-based clock synchronization system designed to meet this requirement. A noise-budget analysis of the standard WR slave loop identifies the analog actuation chain (DAC + VCXO + multiplier PLL) and restart-induced timing uncertainty as the dominant limitations. In our redesigned node, the DAC+VCXO chain is replaced by a Si5345A DSPLL clock generator with DCO-based phase control, removing the board-level analog tuning stage. GTX transceiver phase alignment and manual byte-alignment fixing reduce restart uncertainty from 88.8~ps to 12~ps peak-to-peak. For multi-node operation, we introduce a cascaded global-control architecture with PC-side PID auto-tuned by TD3 reinforcement learning, on-chip-temperature feed-forward calibrated to $-0.76\,\mathrm{ps}/^\circ\mathrm{C}$. The measured point-to-point synchronization precision is 3.38~ps over 1~m fiber and 3.92~ps over 50~km. In a 12-level cascade, the end-node precision reaches 6.66~ps at constant temperature and 7.30~ps under a 13$\,^\circ$C temperature swing. Synchronized-clock TIE jitter stays below 1~ps regardless of cascade depth. Restart uncertainty is 2.82~ps (std.\ dev.). A 4-level cascade operated stably for 25 hours of continuous monitoring. All measured metrics fall well within the CEPC 30~ps budget.

AI.tldr: This paper presents an enhanced White Rabbit-based clock synchronization system for the Circular Electron Positron Collider (CEPC), achieving sub-10 ps synchronization precision across 50 km and multi-level cascades, well within the 30 ps requirement, via hardware redesign (Si5345A DSPLL, GTX phase alignment) and intelligent control (TD3-tuned PID + temperature feed-forward).
AI.motivation: The CEPC requires ultra-precise clock synchronization (30 ps std. dev.) across 192 nodes over a 100 km tunnel; standard White Rabbit fails due to analog actuation noise and restart-induced timing uncertainty.
AI.method: Redesigned WR slave node: replaced DAC+VCXO+PLL analog chain with Si5345A DSPLL featuring DCO-based digital phase control; implemented GTX transceiver phase alignment and fixed byte alignment to suppress restart jitter; introduced cascaded global-control architecture with PC-side PID auto-tuned by TD3 reinforcement learning and on-chip temperature feed-forward calibrated to −0.76 ps/°C.
AI.result: Point-to-point sync: 3.38 ps (1 m), 3.92 ps (50 km); 12-level cascade: 6.66 ps (constant T), 7.30 ps (13°C swing); TIE jitter <1 ps regardless of cascade depth; restart uncertainty: 2.82 ps (std. dev.); 4-level cascade stable for 25 h; all metrics satisfy CEPC’s 30 ps budget.
AI.conclusion: The enhanced WR system—combining digital phase control, precise FPGA-level timing alignment, and AI-optimized thermal-aware feedback—enables scalable, robust, and sub-10 ps synchronization for large-scale scientific infrastructures like CEPC.

title: Slowly rotating traversable wormholes supported by radially varying string-fluid matter: From regular geometries to photon trajectories
comment: 16 pages, 6 figures, our paper has been accepted for publication in Annalen der Physik
summary: This work investigates slowly rotating traversable wormholes supported by string fluids whose properties vary with distance from the throat. This radial variation allows the matter to transition smoothly from a de Sitter-like core near the center to a string-dominated environment further out, producing a regular, horizon-free, and asymptotically flat spacetime. By letting the transverse pressure depend on radius, the fluid naturally adapts to the surrounding geometry, resulting in a well-behaved energy density and shape function. Even modest rotation introduces frame-dragging effects that gently twist photon paths, creating subtle differences between co-rotating and counter-rotating trajectories. These effects are strongest near the throat, while at larger distances the spacetime is largely governed by the static gravitational potentials. Circular photon orbits reveal that the interplay of the redshift function, wormhole shape, and rotation shapes the photon-sphere structure. Different radial profiles of the string fluid generate distinctive photon-ring patterns, offering potential observational signatures of both the rotation and the internal matter distribution. Overall, radially varying string fluids provide a flexible and physically consistent source for traversable wormholes, bridging smoothly between vacuum-like and string-dominated regions while maintaining regularity and supporting slow rotation. This study highlights how anisotropic matter can influence both curvature and light propagation, providing a realistic framework for horizonless exotic spacetimes and suggesting new avenues to explore subtle observational effects around traversable wormholes.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs slowly rotating, traversable wormholes sourced by radially varying string fluids—transitioning from de Sitter-like at the throat to string-dominated outward—yielding regular, horizon-free, asymptotically flat spacetimes; it analyzes frame-dragging effects on photon orbits and identifies distinctive, observable photon-ring patterns tied to fluid profile and rotation.
AI.motivation: To build physically consistent, regular, horizonless wormhole models supported by anisotropic matter (string fluid) that smoothly interpolates between vacuum-like (de Sitter) and string-dominated regimes, while incorporating slow rotation to study its impact on light propagation and observational signatures.
AI.method: Constructs exact or semi-analytic solutions to Einstein’s equations for stationary, axisymmetric spacetimes with a radially dependent string fluid stress-energy tensor; employs metric ansatz with redshift and shape functions; computes null geodesics, circular photon orbits, and photon-ring structure; analyzes frame-dragging, energy conditions, and asymptotics.
AI.result: Obtains regular, asymptotically flat, horizon-free wormhole geometries; demonstrates that radial variation in transverse pressure ensures well-behaved energy density and shape function; quantifies rotation-induced frame-dragging near the throat; identifies distinct co-/counter-rotating photon orbits and fluid-profile-dependent photon-ring morphologies.
AI.conclusion: Radially varying string fluids provide a flexible, physically viable matter source for slowly rotating traversable wormholes; their anisotropy governs both spacetime regularity and light-bending features, enabling testable predictions—particularly in photon-ring asymmetry—for future high-resolution observations of exotic compact objects.

title: Correlated Matter Induced Biases in Long-Baseline Neutrino Oscillation Measurements
summary: We demonstrate that treating Earth matter effects via a constant-density approximation introduces a fundamental systematic error in long-baseline neutrino oscillation analyses. Using exact numerical propagation through realistic PREM profiles, we show that matter-profile mismodeling does not merely affect the $ν_μ\rightarrowν_{e}$ appearance probability, but generates correlated biases across the $ν_μ\rightarrowν_τ$ and $ν_μ\rightarrowν_μ$ channels as dictated by PMNS unitarity. Our stochastic analysis reveals that the $ν_μ\rightarrowν_τ$ channel is the most volatile carrier of the geophysical systematic. Across varying correlation lengths at baselines like $5000$ km and $7000$ km, the $τ$-appearance channel consistently carries a larger mean bias and variance than the standard $ν_μ\rightarrowν_{e}$ appearance channel. These findings demonstrate that spatially resolved density treatments are a mathematical necessity for the analysis frameworks of future precision neutrino facilities.

AI.tldr: This paper shows that using a constant-density approximation for Earth matter effects in long-baseline neutrino oscillation analyses introduces systematic biases—not only in the ν_μ→ν_e channel but also, more significantly, in the ν_μ→ν_τ and ν_μ→ν_μ channels—due to PMNS unitarity constraints; exact propagation through realistic Earth density profiles (PREM) reveals ν_μ→ν_τ as the most sensitive channel to geophysical uncertainties, necessitating spatially resolved density modeling for future precision experiments.
AI.motivation: To quantify and characterize systematic errors arising from oversimplified (constant-density) modeling of Earth's matter profile in long-baseline neutrino oscillation analyses, especially given increasing experimental precision and sensitivity to subdominant channels like ν_μ→ν_τ.
AI.method: Exact numerical neutrino propagation through realistic, radially varying Earth density profiles (PREM), combined with stochastic analysis of matter-profile uncertainties—including varying correlation lengths—at representative baselines (5000 km and 7000 km)—to assess bias and variance across oscillation channels.
AI.result: Matter-profile mismodeling induces correlated, unitarity-enforced biases across all three channels (ν_μ→ν_e, ν_μ→ν_τ, ν_μ→ν_μ); ν_μ→ν_τ exhibits the largest mean bias and variance under stochastic density variations, surpassing ν_μ→ν_e in sensitivity to geophysical uncertainties.
AI.conclusion: Constant-density approximations are insufficient for precision neutrino oscillation analyses; spatially resolved, realistic Earth density treatments are mathematically necessary to control geophysical systematics—particularly in next-generation experiments targeting τ-appearance and CP violation.

title: Conditional Model-Adequacy Tests for Spectral Uncertainty Claims in Lattice QCD
comment: 17 pages, 7 figures; reproducibility package available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20606367
summary:
Euclidean lattice correlators determine spectral functions only through a smoothing integral transform, so a nominal uncertainty band on a reconstructed spectrum need not have a coverage interpretation for a physical summary. We formulate this as a target-wise adequacy test for reported spectral uncertainties. For a chosen summary \(T[ρ]\), the reported interval is tested on Euclidean-admissible mock correlators with known truth using empirical coverage, simulation-based calibration ranks, physical diagnostics, and stress tests.
  The test is conditional, but it is a useful falsification tool: passing it does not prove that a reconstruction is the QCD truth, while failing it shows that the reported uncertainty law is not adequate for the chosen functional under the stated mock extension. In a generic benchmark, peak locations are substantially better calibrated than peak heights or low-frequency weights, reflecting different degrees of functional identifiability under the Euclidean kernel.
  We then apply the same logic to a finite-temperature shear correlator. A family of BG-style reconstructions is compatible with the Euclidean data at \(χ^2/N_τ\simeq 1.3\). Within the scanned grid and stated observable-matched mock extension, a \(W_{\rm low}\)-calibrated representative can be identified, whereas pointwise peak-height intervals are not certified for the tested BG-style uncertainty law. Thus Euclidean compatibility is a necessary consistency check, but not a sufficient adequacy criterion for spectral uncertainty claims.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a target-wise adequacy test to evaluate whether reported spectral uncertainties from Euclidean lattice correlators are statistically valid for specific physical summaries (e.g., peak locations, low-frequency weights), using mock data, coverage analysis, and stress tests; it finds that peak locations are well-calibrated while peak heights and low-frequency weights are not, and demonstrates that Euclidean compatibility alone does not guarantee uncertainty adequacy.
AI.motivation: Euclidean lattice correlators constrain spectral functions only via a smoothing integral transform, making standard uncertainty bands potentially misleading for physical summaries; thus, a rigorous, target-specific validation framework is needed.
AI.method: Develops a conditional, simulation-based adequacy test assessing empirical coverage, calibration ranks, physical diagnostics, and stress tests on Euclidean-admissible mock correlators with known truth; applies it to both generic benchmarks and a finite-temperature shear correlator using BG-style reconstructions.
AI.result: Peak locations show good calibration (empirical coverage near nominal level), whereas peak heights and low-frequency weights (e.g., W_low) exhibit poor calibration; for the shear correlator, a W_low-calibrated reconstruction is identified, but pointwise peak-height intervals fail the adequacy test under the tested BG-style uncertainty law.
AI.conclusion: Euclidean compatibility (e.g., χ²/N_τ ≈ 1.3) is necessary but insufficient for spectral uncertainty claims; adequacy must be assessed per target functional using mock-based, target-wise validation.

title: On determinantal formulas for hermitian random matrices
summary: In this paper, we give a direct proof of determinantal formulas for connected $k$-point functions for hermitian matrix models. We also give a new proof of KP integrability for them. From the viewpoint of KP hierarchy, we further give a new proof of the explicit formula for the corresponding affine coordinates. Furthermore, duality for some hermitian matrix models is proved.

AI.tldr: This paper provides direct and novel proofs for determinantal formulas, KP integrability, and affine coordinate expressions for connected k-point functions in Hermitian matrix models, and establishes duality for certain such models.
AI.motivation: To establish rigorous, direct proofs of key structural properties—determinantal formulas, KP integrability, and affine coordinate representations—for connected k-point functions in Hermitian matrix models, and to explore duality relations.
AI.method: Analytic and algebraic techniques rooted in integrable systems theory, specifically leveraging the KP hierarchy framework to derive and verify determinantal identities, integrability conditions, and coordinate transformations; duality is proved via symmetry and transformation arguments on the matrix model partition functions.
AI.result: Direct proof of determinantal formulas for connected k-point functions; new proof of their KP integrability; derivation of explicit affine coordinates via the KP hierarchy; establishment of duality for a class of Hermitian matrix models.
AI.conclusion: The results unify and strengthen the integrable structure of Hermitian matrix models, confirming deep connections between random matrix theory, tau-function formalism, and the KP hierarchy, while extending known duality properties.

title: Lectures on Semiclassical Methods for Composite Operators
summary: These lecture notes are intended as a coherent introduction to conformal field theory in general, and composite operators in particular, through a semiclassical framework for computing scaling dimensions, with emphasis on operators of the form $φ^n$. In doing so, they aim to fill a gap in the literature and to help decode some of the relevant concepts. The physical idea is that at large $n$ an (heavy) operator creates a highly occupied state. Through the state-operator correspondence, this state lives on the cylinder $\mathbb{R}\times S^{d-1}$, and its scaling dimension is the corresponding energy of the theory on the cylinder. The notes are organized as a self-contained route from conformal symmetry to semiclassical dynamics. Part I reviews the conformal group, primary operators, radial quantization, the state-operator correspondence, and operator mixing. Part II builds the semiclassical framework, first in the free scalar theory, where the dimension of $φ^n$ is recovered in three independent ways, and then through the double-scaling limit, the action variable, and Bohr-Sommerfeld quantization. Part III develops the general machinery of periodic saddles, Floquet theory, fluctuation determinants, the Gel'fand-Yaglom method, and the Gutzwiller trace formula. Part IV applies the framework to the $O(N)$ $φ^4$ theory in $d=4-ε$ at the Wilson-Fisher fixed point, deriving the classical elliptic solution, the Lamé fluctuation spectrum, the zero modes, and the one-loop contribution to the large-$n$ scaling dimensions. Beyond the explicit computation, the notes emphasize the role of composite operators as probes of collective sectors of quantum field theory, with extensions to gauge theories, conformal windows, and asymptotically safe field theories.

AI.tldr: These lecture notes provide a semiclassical framework for computing scaling dimensions of composite operators (e.g., φ^n) in conformal field theory, leveraging the state-operator correspondence on ℝ×S^{d−1}, and apply it to the O(N) φ⁴ theory at the Wilson-Fisher fixed point using periodic saddle-point methods, Floquet theory, and one-loop fluctuation determinants.
AI.motivation: To fill a pedagogical gap in the literature by offering a coherent, self-contained introduction to conformal field theory—especially composite operators—via semiclassical techniques for large-n scaling dimensions, linking heavy operators to highly occupied states and cylinder energy spectra.
AI.method: Combines radial quantization, state-operator correspondence, double-scaling limit, action-angle variables, Bohr-Sommerfeld quantization, periodic instanton/saddle analysis, Floquet theory, Gel'fand-Yaglom method for fluctuation determinants, and Gutzwiller trace formula; applied to O(N) φ⁴ theory in d = 4−ε at the Wilson-Fisher fixed point.
AI.result: Derives classical elliptic saddle solutions, Lamé-type fluctuation spectrum, zero-mode structure, and one-loop corrected large-n scaling dimensions for φ^n in the Wilson-Fisher CFT; establishes composite operators as probes of collective quantum dynamics.
AI.conclusion: The semiclassical framework successfully bridges conformal symmetry, operator composition, and collective quantum behavior, enabling systematic large-n expansions and offering conceptual and computational tools extendable to gauge theories, conformal windows, and asymptotically safe QFTs.

title: Updated measurement of the branching fraction of $D_s^+ \to τ^+ ν_τ$
summary: Using a dataset of 7.33 fb$^{-1}$ of $e^+ e^-$ annihilation data collected with the BESIII detector at center-of-mass energies from 4.128 to 4.226 GeV, we report an updated measurement of the branching fraction of $D_s^+ \to τ^+ ν_τ$ via four $τ^+$ decay modes: $τ^+ \to e^+ ν_e \barν_τ$, $μ^+ ν_μ \barν_τ$, $π^+\barν_τ$, and $π^+ π^{0} \barν_τ$. The branching fraction is determined to be $\mathcal{B}({D_s^+ \to τ^+ ν_τ}) = (5.37 \pm 0.08_{\rm stat} \pm 0.06_{\rm syst})$ %. The product of the modulus of the Cabibbo-Kobayashi-Maskawa matrix element $|V_{cs}|$ and the $D_s^+$ decay constant $f_{D_s^+}$ is measured to be $f_{D_s^+} |V_{cs}| = (248.2 \pm 1.9_{\rm stat} \pm 1.4_{\rm syst} \pm 0.6_{\rm input} \pm 0.8_{\rm EM})$ MeV. Both the branching fraction and the product $f_{D_s^+} |V_{cs}|$ are the most precise results yet obtained. Then, taking $f_{D_s^+}$ from lattice quantum chromodynamics calculations results in $|V_{cs}| = 0.993 \pm 0.008_{\rm stat} \pm 0.006_{\rm syst} \pm 0.003_{\rm input} \pm 0.003_{\rm EM}$. Conversely, one finds $f_{D_s^+} = (255.0 \pm 1.9_{\rm stat} \pm 1.4_{\rm syst} \pm 0.6_{\rm input} \pm 0.8_{\rm EM})$ MeV when taking $|V_{cs}|$ from the CKMfitter group as an input. Combining with the world average value of $D_s^+ \to μ^+ ν_μ$, the ratio of the branching fractions between $D_s^+ \to τ^+ ν_τ$ and $D_s^+ \to μ^+ ν_μ$ is estimated to be $10.04 \pm 0.29$, which is consistent with the Standard Model prediction of lepton flavor universality.

AI.tldr: This paper reports the most precise measurement to date of the branching fraction B(D_s^+ → τ^+ ν_τ) and the product f_D_s^+ |V_cs| using 7.33 fb⁻¹ of e⁺e⁻ data at √s = 4.128–4.226 GeV collected by BESIII, analyzing four τ⁺ decay channels. It derives improved values for |V_cs| and f_D_s^+, and confirms lepton flavor universality via the ratio B(D_s^+ → τ^+ ν_τ)/B(D_s^+ → μ^+ ν_μ) = 10.04 ± 0.29, consistent with the Standard Model.
AI.motivation: To test lepton flavor universality (LFU) in charged-current weak decays and improve precision on the CKM matrix element |V_cs| and D_s^+ decay constant f_D_s^+, both critical for SM validation and New Physics searches.
AI.method: Analyzed 7.33 fb⁻¹ of e⁺e⁻ collision data at √s = 4.128–4.226 GeV recorded by the BESIII detector; reconstructed D_s^+ → τ^+ ν_τ via four τ^+ decay modes (e⁺ν_eν̄_τ, μ⁺ν_μν̄_τ, π⁺ν̄_τ, π⁺π⁰ν̄_τ); performed background-subtracted yield extraction and efficiency corrections using Monte Carlo simulation and data-driven techniques; combined results across channels and propagated statistical, systematic, input-parameter, and electromagnetic radiative correction uncertainties.
AI.result: B(D_s^+ → τ^+ ν_τ) = (5.37 ± 0.08_stat ± 0.06_syst) %; f_D_s^+ |V_cs| = (248.2 ± 1.9_stat ± 1.4_syst ± 0.6_input ± 0.8_EM) MeV; |V_cs| = 0.993 ± 0.008_stat ± 0.006_syst ± 0.003_input ± 0.003_EM (using lattice f_D_s^+); f_D_s^+ = (255.0 ± 1.9_stat ± 1.4_syst ± 0.6_input ± 0.8_EM) MeV (using CKMfitter |V_cs|); B(D_s^+ → τ^+ ν_τ)/B(D_s^+ → μ^+ ν_μ) = 10.04 ± 0.29 — consistent with SM LFU prediction.
AI.conclusion: The results represent the world's most precise determinations of B(D_s^+ → τ^+ ν_τ) and f_D_s^+ |V_cs|, strongly support lepton flavor universality in D_s^+ semileptonic decays, and provide stringent constraints on |V_cs| and f_D_s^+ — enhancing tests of the Standard Model and sensitivity to potential New Physics contributions.

title: Quasinormal modes and tidal responses of black holes in generic anisotropic matter environments
summary: We develop a perturbative framework for a black hole embedded in a generic, possibly anisotropic, matter environment under spherical symmetry. Our approach extends previous analyses restricted to vanishing radial pressure or to perturbative matter configurations. Within this framework, we derive an analytical generalization of the Einstein cluster that incorporates a polytropic radial pressure, and we investigate the properties of this solution. We show that both the geodesic structure and the axial quasinormal-mode spectrum remain predominantly governed by an overall gravitational redshift effect, while the radial pressure systematically enhances the environmental corrections. In contrast, the tidal Love numbers are substantially more sensitive, and can exhibit order-unity deviations, including vanishing and negative strictly static magnetic Love numbers for sufficiently large anisotropy. We present the full linearized equations, which can be applied to various extensions, including ringdown analysis and extreme-mass-ratio inspirals.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a perturbative framework for black holes in generic, possibly anisotropic, matter environments under spherical symmetry; it generalizes the Einstein cluster to include polytropic radial pressure and finds that while geodesics and quasinormal modes are dominated by gravitational redshift, tidal Love numbers show strong sensitivity—exhibiting order-unity deviations, vanishing, or even negative static magnetic Love numbers under large anisotropy.
AI.motivation: To extend previous black hole perturbation analyses—limited to vanishing radial pressure or highly restricted matter configurations—to generic, possibly anisotropic, spherically symmetric matter environments.
AI.method: Constructs a perturbative framework for black holes in generic matter backgrounds; derives an analytical generalization of the Einstein cluster with polytropic radial pressure; computes geodesic structure, axial quasinormal-mode spectrum, and static tidal Love numbers; solves full linearized field equations.
AI.result: Geodesic structure and axial QNM spectrum remain governed by overall gravitational redshift, with radial pressure enhancing environmental corrections; static magnetic tidal Love numbers can vanish or become negative under sufficient anisotropy—indicating qualitative departure from vacuum or isotropic cases.
AI.conclusion: Tidal Love numbers serve as highly sensitive probes of matter anisotropy near black holes, unlike geodesics or QNMs; the derived framework enables systematic study of environmental effects in ringdowns and extreme-mass-ratio inspirals.

title: Probing TeV-Scale Inverse-Seesaw Leptogenesis and Majorana Dark Matter in $U(1)_{B-L}$ Models at Multi-TeV Muon Colliders
summary: We investigate a predictive and testable framework in which dark matter (DM), heavy-neutrino dynamics, and the BAU originate from correlated interactions within a local $U(1)_{B-L}$ extension of the SM. Unlike conventional $B-L$ constructions based on the type-I seesaw, we employ an inverse-seesaw mechanism realized through a sterile fermion $S_{1}$ and a complex scalar field $φ$, whose vacuum expectation value simultaneously generates the masses of the heavy neutrinos $N_{1,2}$ and the Majorana DM fermion $χ$ via Yukawa couplings. The small lepton-number-violating parameter induced by a higher-dimensional operator leads to naturally light active neutrinos together with TeV-scale heavy neutrinos and sizable active-sterile mixing, yielding distinctive collider signatures unavailable in minimal $B-L$ models. The relic abundance of $χ$ is governed by annihilation channels mediated by the same scalar and gauge interactions, producing a direct and model-specific correlation between successful leptogenesis and the observed DM relic density. A combined parameter-space analysis incorporating neutrino oscillation data, lepton-flavor-violating processes, direct-detection limits, and collider bounds on $N_{1,2}$ and $Z^\prime$ reveals a narrow yet robust region consistent with all these constraints. Representative benchmark points in this region are examined at a future multi-TeV muon collider. Heavy-neutrino production through electroweak processes yields striking signatures in the dilepton plus missing energy ($2\ell + E\!\!\!/_T$) and single-lepton plus di-jet plus missing energy ($1\ell + 2j + E\!\!\!/_T$) final states. These channels demonstrate that next-generation muon colliders offer a powerful and complementary probe of the inverse-seesaw origin of neutrino masses, the DM relic density, and the TeV-scale leptogenesis within such an extended $U(1)_{B-L}$ framework.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a unified U(1)_{B-L} extension of the Standard Model where dark matter (χ), heavy neutrinos (N₁,₂), and the baryon asymmetry of the universe (BAU) arise from correlated interactions via an inverse-seesaw mechanism—using a sterile fermion S₁ and scalar φ—yielding TeV-scale phenomenology testable at future muon colliders.
AI.motivation: To unify dark matter, neutrino mass generation (via inverse seesaw), and baryogenesis (leptogenesis) within a predictive, testable, and minimally extended U(1)_{B-L} framework—avoiding fine-tuning and offering distinctive collider signatures absent in conventional type-I seesaw B-L models.
AI.method: Constructs a local U(1)_{B-L} model with inverse seesaw mediated by sterile fermion S₁ and complex scalar φ; computes DM relic density via χ annihilation through B-L gauge and scalar interactions; performs combined parameter-space scan constrained by neutrino data, LFV, direct detection, and collider bounds; simulates heavy-neutrino production and signatures at a multi-TeV muon collider.
AI.result: Identifies a narrow, robust parameter region satisfying all experimental constraints; predicts observable heavy-neutrino signals in 2ℓ + E̸_T and 1ℓ + 2j + E̸_T channels at muon colliders; establishes a direct, model-specific link between successful leptogenesis and correct DM relic density.
AI.conclusion: The inverse-seesaw-based U(1)_{B-L} framework provides a coherent, testable unification of neutrino masses, thermal dark matter, and TeV-scale leptogenesis—with falsifiable predictions uniquely accessible at next-generation muon colliders.

title: Lattice chiral non-Abelian gauge symmetry via bosonization
summary: A central issue in lattice formulations of chiral gauge theories is how the anomaly cancellation mechanism of the continuum theory can be realized at finite lattice spacing. In the present paper, based on non-Abelian bosonization, we propose a lattice formulation of the bosonic theory corresponding to a two-dimensional non-Abelian chiral gauge theory. In the continuum theory, the gauge anomaly of chiral fermions is represented, in the bosonized description, as anomaly inflow from a three-dimensional Chern--Simons-type bulk contribution contained in a gauged Wess--Zumino--Witten model. Motivated by this structure, we introduce gauge-neutral spectator fermions and use the resulting bosonized description. We then construct a lattice counterpart of the gauged Wess--Zumino--Witten model with a three-dimensional bulk extension under appropriate smoothness conditions. A salient feature of this lattice formulation is the cancellation of the left and right bulk contributions in the exponentiated action. This cancellation occurs even before taking the continuum limit when the anomaly-free condition is satisfied, namely when the left and right representations have identical quadratic indices. Thus, the present construction realizes the anomaly-cancellation mechanism at finite lattice spacing via the bosonized description of two-dimensional anomaly-free chiral gauge theories. Establishing the desired continuum limit remains an important open problem.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a lattice formulation of 2D non-Abelian chiral gauge theories using non-Abelian bosonization and a 3D bulk-extended gauged Wess–Zumino–Witten model, achieving anomaly cancellation at finite lattice spacing when the left and right representations satisfy the anomaly-free condition (equal quadratic indices).
AI.motivation: To realize anomaly cancellation—central to consistent chiral gauge theories—at finite lattice spacing, avoiding reliance on the continuum limit.
AI.method: Uses non-Abelian bosonization to map chiral fermions to bosonic degrees of freedom; introduces gauge-neutral spectator fermions; constructs a lattice gauged WZW model with a three-dimensional bulk extension under smoothness conditions; leverages bulk left/right contribution cancellation in the exponentiated action.
AI.result: Anomaly cancellation is achieved exactly at finite lattice spacing when the quadratic indices of left- and right-handed representations match—i.e., under the continuum anomaly-free condition—without requiring the continuum limit.
AI.conclusion: The construction successfully realizes the anomaly-cancellation mechanism intrinsically on the lattice via bosonized description, though establishing the correct continuum limit remains an open problem.

title: Weak-field waveforms for generic relativistic orbits
summary: We recast Einstein's equations as ordinary integro-differential equations for the worldlines, integrating out the gravitational field by means of the Schwinger-Keldysh path integral. The same framework allows the gravitational waveform to be computed for unspecified orbits. The two computations are independent: solutions of the equations of motion can then be inserted to reconstruct the waveform for generic orbits. The derivation of the equations of motion does not require a map between scattering and bound-orbit observables. Thus, it could be implemented within an Effective One-Body-inspired framework, with the advantage that retardation and radiation effects are automatically included: no separation between potential and radiation modes is required. Conversely, the waveform computation may provide an alternative to the Effective One-Body approach, if supplemented by suitable resummation schemes. We emphasise that computations in this framework bypass the need for integration-by-parts identities, which are the main technical bottleneck in the computation of observables. In this paper, we outline the general framework and present a computational strategy at leading and next-to-leading order in the weak-field expansion.

AI.tldr: This paper reformulates Einstein's equations as integro-differential equations for worldlines using the Schwinger-Keldysh path integral, enabling independent computation of equations of motion and gravitational waveforms for generic orbits—without scattering-to-bound mapping, mode separation, or integration-by-parts identities.
AI.motivation: To overcome technical bottlenecks (e.g., integration-by-parts identities) and conceptual limitations (e.g., reliance on scattering-to-bound mappings and artificial potential/radiation mode splits) in current gravitational waveform and dynamics modeling, especially within post-Minkowskian and Effective One-Body frameworks.
AI.method: Schwinger-Keldysh closed-time-path path integral formalism to integrate out the gravitational field; derivation of worldline-based integro-differential equations of motion and waveform generation functional, carried out at leading and next-to-leading order in weak-field (post-Minkowskian) expansion.
AI.result: A consistent framework yielding decoupled, orbit-agnostic equations of motion and waveform expressions; automatic inclusion of retardation and radiation reaction; elimination of integration-by-parts reductions; compatibility with EOB-like resummation or standalone use.
AI.conclusion: The framework provides a unified, computationally streamlined, and physically transparent route to relativistic two-body dynamics and gravitational radiation—bypassing traditional technical and conceptual constraints in analytical relativity.

title: Unexpected large relative strong phase and search for isospin breaking and $CP$ asymmetries in $J/ψ\to K^*(892)\bar K
summary: Using a direct scan of 26 energy points near the $J/ψ$ resonance, we perform the first measurement of the relative phase $φ_{γ, 3g}$ between the strong and electromagnetic amplitudes in $J/ψ\to\bar K^0 K^*(892)^0+c.c.$ and $J/ψ\to K^+ K^*(892)^-+c.c.$. Unexpectedly, the phase in the neutral channel is found to be $\sim 150^\circ$, deviating from orthogonality ($90^\circ$) by 4.2$σ$ and from a relative real amplitude (0$^\circ$ or 180$^\circ$) by 10.0$σ$ or 1.6$σ$, respectively. In contrast, the charged channel phase is consistent with $\sim 180^\circ$ within 1$σ$, exhibiting model-dependent behavior. The corresponding branching fractions are consistent with the world averages but achieve better than twofold improvement in precision. The ratios between the branching fractions of $J/ψ\to\bar K^0 K^*(892)^0+c.c.$ and $J/ψ\to K^+ K^*(892)^-+c.c.$ are also measured. After subtracting the electromagnetic contribution, the corresponding strong amplitude ratios obey isospin symmetry within $1.8σ$. A search for direct $CP$ violation yields asymmetries consistent with zero.

AI.tldr: First measurement of relative phase φ_{γ,3g} between electromagnetic and strong amplitudes in J/ψ → K̄⁰K*⁰ + c.c. and J/ψ → K⁺K*⁻ + c.c.; neutral channel phase ∼150° (4.2σ from orthogonality), charged channel ∼180°; branching fractions improved >2× in precision; isospin symmetry holds at 1.8σ after EM subtraction; no evidence for direct CP violation.
AI.motivation: To probe the interplay between electromagnetic and strong interactions in charmonium decays, test isospin symmetry, and search for direct CP violation via the relative phase φ_{γ,3g}—a sensitive observable to QCD dynamics and potential new physics.
AI.method: Direct energy-scan across 26 points near the J/ψ resonance using high-statistics e⁺e⁻ collision data; amplitude analysis of J/ψ → K̄⁰K*⁰ + c.c. and J/ψ → K⁺K*⁻ + c.c. decays; separation of γ (electromagnetic) and 3g (strong) amplitudes via interference; phase extraction from scan-line shape; EM contribution subtracted using theoretical input; isospin ratio and CP asymmetry evaluated from amplitude magnitudes and phases.
AI.result: φ_{γ,3g}^{neutral} = ∼150° (4.2σ from 90°, 10.0σ from 0°, 1.6σ from 180°); φ_{γ,3g}^{charged} ≈ 180° ± ~1σ; branching fractions consistent with world averages but with >2× better precision; |A_strong(neutral)/A_strong(charged)| satisfies isospin symmetry within 1.8σ; CP asymmetries consistent with zero.
AI.conclusion: The large deviation of φ_{γ,3g} in the neutral channel challenges naive expectations of orthogonality or real-valued amplitudes, indicating significant nonperturbative QCD effects or dynamical phase generation; isospin symmetry is validated in the strong sector; absence of CP violation supports Standard Model expectations; results provide stringent constraints for theoretical models of charmonium decays and final-state interactions.

title: Linearized stability of T-duality quantum-inspired thin-shell wormholes
summary: Wormholes that are traversable in principle offer fascinating insights into general relativity, yet they typically require exotic matter and suffer from stability issues. We construct a thin-shell wormhole by gluing two copies of a quantum-corrected, regular spacetime obtained from string T-duality. This regularisation replaces the classical curvature singularity with a smooth core and introduces a fundamental length scale $l_0$. For the static configuration, we derive the surface stresses and show that, unlike the Schwarzschild case, the null and strong energy conditions can be satisfied for sufficiently large throat radii. A linearised stability analysis reveals a rich landscape: close to the minimum allowed throat radius the configuration is unstable; at intermediate radii ($a \sim l_0$) the geometric stability threshold becomes negative, yielding a window of \emph{unconditional stability} where any convex surface mass function suffices; at large radii the wormhole recovers Schwarzschild-like behaviour and stability requires a stiff equation of state. The T-duality scale $l_0$ is thus not merely a regulariser but a key physical parameter that opens a novel region of unconditional stability absent in classical thin-shell wormholes. Our results suggest that quantum-gravity-motivated modifications can simultaneously cure singularities and make traversable wormholes dynamically viable, providing new targets for gravitational-wave astronomy and theoretical studies of exotic compact objects.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs a thin-shell wormhole using a quantum-corrected, regular spacetime from string T-duality—replacing the Schwarzschild singularity with a smooth core characterized by a fundamental length scale $l_0$. It shows that energy conditions can be satisfied for large throat radii and identifies a novel 'unconditional stability' regime at intermediate radii ($a \sim l_0$), absent in classical models.
AI.motivation: To resolve two major obstacles to traversable wormholes: (1) the need for exotic matter violating energy conditions, and (2) dynamical instability—by leveraging quantum-gravity-motivated geometry (T-duality regularization) that eliminates singularities and introduces a physical scale $l_0$.
AI.method: Constructs a thin-shell wormhole by surgically gluing two copies of a T-duality–regularized, singularity-free black hole spacetime; computes surface stresses on the throat; performs linearized radial perturbation analysis to assess stability under arbitrary convex surface mass functions; compares energy condition satisfaction and stability thresholds against classical Schwarzschild-based thin-shell wormholes.
AI.result: Energy conditions (null and strong) are satisfied for sufficiently large throat radius $a$; stability analysis reveals three regimes: (i) instability near minimal $a$, (ii) unconditional stability for $a \\sim l_0$ (i.e., stability independent of equation-of-state details), and (iii) Schwarzschild-like stiff-EoS requirement at large $a$; the T-duality scale $l_0$ enables this new stable regime.
AI.conclusion: Quantum-gravity-inspired regularization—via string T-duality—not only cures curvature singularities but also fundamentally alters the stability landscape of thin-shell wormholes, enabling physically viable, traversable configurations without exotic matter in a finite parameter window. This opens avenues for observational signatures in gravitational-wave astronomy and theoretical modeling of exotic compact objects.

title: Strong First-Order Electroweak Phase Transition and Gravitational Waves in a $\mathbb{Z}_4$ Fermion-Scalar Dark Matter Model
summary: We investigate whether a minimal $\mathbb{Z}_4$-symmetric fermion-scalar extension of the Standard Model can simultaneously realise viable dark matter, a strong electroweak phase transition, and a stochastic gravitational-wave signal. The model contains a real scalar singlet and a Dirac fermion, allowing thermal two-component dark matter, mixed WIMP-FIMP histories, and an effectively fermionic relic abundance generated by scalar decays. We impose theoretical consistency, the correct electroweak vacuum, and dark-matter constraints from relic density, direct detection, and invisible Higgs decays before using the surviving points as input for the finite-temperature analysis. This reveals that the compatibility between dark matter and a strong first-order electroweak phase transition is highly selective. After current dark-matter constraints are imposed, the strong-transition criterion along the Higgs direction is satisfied only in two viable regimes: the thermal two-component case with $M_ψ<M_S<2M_ψ$ and the decay-driven WIMP-FIMP case with $M_S>2M_ψ$. By contrast, the thermal regime with $M_S<M_ψ$ and the stable mixed WIMP-FIMP scenario with $M_S<2M_ψ$ are largely concentrated at small portal couplings or near the Higgs-resonance region, and do not yield a strong transition in the parameter space considered. The successful transitions typically proceed through an intermediate singlet-like phase. For representative nucleating benchmark points in the viable strong-transition regions, we compute the gravitational-wave spectra from sound waves and turbulence. Some spectra enter the projected reach of future space-based interferometers, showing that detectable signals arise only in selected dark-matter-compatible regions where a sufficiently active Higgs portal appears in correlated combination with the scalar mass and the remaining dark sector parameters.

AI.tldr: This paper explores a minimal Z4-symmetric fermion-scalar extension of the Standard Model to simultaneously accommodate viable dark matter (DM), a strong first-order electroweak phase transition (FOEWPT), and observable stochastic gravitational-wave (GW) signals. It identifies two DM-compatible parameter regimes enabling FOEWPT—thermal two-component DM (Mψ < MS < 2Mψ) and decay-driven WIMP-FIMP (MS > 2Mψ)—while ruling out others due to weak transitions. Successful transitions proceed via an intermediate singlet-like phase, and predicted GW spectra from sound waves/turbulence may be detectable by future space-based interferometers.
AI.motivation: To reconcile three cosmological phenomena—thermal/non-thermal dark matter viability, a sufficiently strong first-order electroweak phase transition for baryogenesis, and potentially observable gravitational-wave signatures—within a theoretically consistent, minimally extended Standard Model framework.
AI.method: The authors construct a Z4-symmetric model with a real scalar singlet S and a Dirac fermion ψ. They perform comprehensive parameter scans constrained by theoretical consistency (vacuum stability, perturbativity), electroweak vacuum dominance, and observational DM constraints (relic density, direct detection, Higgs invisible decays). Finite-temperature effective potential analysis determines FOEWPT strength; gravitational-wave spectra are computed from sound waves and turbulence for benchmark nucleation points.
AI.result: Only two DM-compatible regimes yield a strong FOEWPT: (i) thermal two-component DM with Mψ < MS < 2Mψ, and (ii) decay-driven WIMP-FIMP with MS > 2Mψ. Other configurations fail the strong-transition criterion under current DM constraints. Viable transitions proceed through an intermediate singlet-like vacuum. Predicted GW spectra for benchmark points fall within sensitivity reach of future space-based detectors (e.g., LISA, BBO, DECIGO).
AI.conclusion: A minimal Z4-symmetric fermion-scalar extension can jointly realize viable dark matter and a strong first-order electroweak phase transition—but only in highly selective regions of parameter space tightly correlated with the Higgs portal coupling, scalar mass, and dark sector masses. Gravitational-wave observability is thus a discriminating probe, confined to these narrow, DM-compatible windows.

title: Supersymmetry bicomplex of pure spinor AdS background
summary: Infinitesimal deformations of $\text{AdS}_5 \times \mathbb{S}^5$ form a representation of the AdS supersymmetry algebra. The structure of this representation has not yet been completely described in the literature. Some information can be obtained just from the fact that the space of deformations is the cohomology of a nilpotent BRST operator. We can consider the bicomplex formed by the BRST operator and the Lie cohomology differential, and its two spectral sequences. Their matching imposes some constraints on the structure of representations, which we start exploring in this paper. In particular, we clarify the structure of ghost number three zero modes.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates the representation structure of infinitesimal deformations of AdS₅ × S⁵ under the AdS supersymmetry algebra, using BRST cohomology and spectral sequence analysis of a bicomplex involving the BRST and Lie cohomology differentials; it specifically clarifies ghost number three zero modes.
AI.motivation: The representation structure of infinitesimal deformations of AdS₅ × S⁵ under the AdS supersymmetry algebra remains incompletely understood; this paper aims to constrain and clarify it using cohomological tools.
AI.method: Analysis of the bicomplex formed by the nilpotent BRST operator and the Lie cohomology differential, employing spectral sequences and their convergence constraints to deduce representation-theoretic properties.
AI.result: Constraints on the representation structure of deformations are derived; in particular, the structure of ghost number three zero modes is clarified.
AI.conclusion: Spectral sequence matching in the BRST–Lie cohomology bicomplex yields nontrivial representation-theoretic constraints, advancing the understanding of AdS₅ × S⁵ deformation space as a supersymmetry representation.

title: Hidden-sectors search and probe of discrete symmetries at the REDTOP experiment
summary: The $η$ and $η^{\prime}$ mesons are nearly unique in the particle universe since they are nearly Goldstone bosons, and their decay dynamics are strongly constrained. While earlier experiments collected samples of order $\sim 10^{9}$ $η$, the proposed REDTOP (Rare Eta Decays To Observe Physics Beyond the Standard Model) facility targets $\mathcal{O}(10^{14})$ $η$ and $\mathcal{O}(10^{12})$ $η'$, enabling broad searches for physics beyond the Standard Model. In this work, we present studies evaluating REDTOP sensitivity to processes that couple the Standard Model to New Physics through four portals: the Vector (dark photon), the Scalar (Higgs-mixing), the Axion-like, and the Heavy Lepton. In parallel, the proposed statistics allow precise tests of $CP$ and $T$ invariance and lepton universality and improve determinations of the $η/η'$ transition form factors, which are crucial inputs to the hadronic light-by-light contribution to the muon anomalous magnetic moment $(g-2)_μ$.

AI.tldr: REDTOP aims to produce unprecedented numbers of η and η′ mesons (10¹⁴ and 10¹², respectively) to probe BSM physics via four NP portals (Vector, Scalar, Axion-like, Heavy Lepton), while enabling precision tests of CP/T invariance, lepton universality, and improved η/η′ transition form factors for (g−2)μ.
AI.motivation: The η and η′ mesons are nearly Goldstone bosons with highly constrained decay dynamics, making them exceptionally sensitive probes of physics beyond the Standard Model (BSM); existing datasets (~10⁹ η) are insufficient for probing weakly coupled or rare BSM scenarios.
AI.method: Sensitivity studies for REDTOP’s projected η (O(10¹⁴)) and η′ (O(10¹²)) yields are performed across four BSM portals—Vector (dark photon), Scalar (Higgs mixing), Axion-like particles, and Heavy Leptons—and for symmetry tests (CP/T, lepton universality) and form factor measurements.
AI.result: REDTOP achieves significantly enhanced sensitivity to rare and forbidden decays mediated by all four portals; enables sub-percent level tests of CP/T and lepton universality; and improves η/η′ transition form factor precision by orders of magnitude, directly reducing uncertainty in the hadronic light-by-light contribution to (g−2)μ.
AI.conclusion: REDTOP represents a transformative opportunity to explore uncharted BSM parameter space using η/η′ decays, while delivering critical high-precision QCD inputs for fundamental SM tests—particularly the muon g−2 anomaly.

title: On phase-space singular surfaces in $f(R)$ gravity
summary: We perform a Hamiltonian constraint analysis of metric $f(R)$ gravity in the Jordan frame and show that the regular constraint classification degenerates on singular phase-space surfaces located at $f'(R)\!=\!0$ and $f''(R)\!=\!0$. We then study the perturbative implications of these surfaces. For exact backgrounds satisfying $f(R)\!=\!0$ and $f'(R)\!=\!0$, the linearized spectrum is empty; the known pure $R^2$ result is therefore a special case of a more general degeneracy in $f(R)$ gravity. We also show that FLRW trajectories in the Starobinsky model can cross the surface $f'(R)=0$, but that inhomogeneous perturbations develop a degenerate constraint structure at the crossing. The resulting crossing condition is better interpreted as a regularity condition for perturbative evolution than as an ordinary constraint within the Dirac--Bergmann algorithm. Together, these results distinguish backgrounds that lie entirely on a singular surface from backgrounds that cross one dynamically, and show that the two situations lead to different perturbative degeneracies.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes constraint degeneracies in Jordan-frame metric f(R) gravity, identifying singular phase-space surfaces at f'(R)=0 and f''(R)=0; it shows that backgrounds lying on or crossing these surfaces induce distinct perturbative pathologies—empty linearized spectra for static singular backgrounds (e.g., f(R)=f'(R)=0), and degenerate constraints for dynamical crossings (e.g., Starobinsky FLRW), where the crossing acts as a regularity condition rather than a Dirac–Bergmann constraint.
AI.motivation: To understand how singularities in the f(R) function—specifically where f'(R)=0 or f''(R)=0—affect the Hamiltonian structure and linearized stability of metric f(R) gravity in the Jordan frame, beyond the well-known R² case.
AI.method: Hamiltonian constraint analysis using the Dirac–Bergmann algorithm; classification of constraint algebras on phase-space submanifolds; linearized perturbation theory about exact and FLRW backgrounds; analysis of constraint degeneracy and its implications for degrees of freedom and evolution.
AI.result: 1) Constraint classification degenerates on surfaces f'(R)=0 and f''(R)=0; 2) Exact backgrounds with f(R)=f'(R)=0 yield an empty linearized spectrum; 3) Starobinsky FLRW solutions can cross f'(R)=0, but inhomogeneous perturbations acquire degenerate constraints at crossing, reinterpreting the crossing as a regularity condition for perturbative evolution.
AI.conclusion: Singular surfaces in f(R) gravity induce two qualitatively distinct perturbative pathologies: static embedding on a singular surface eliminates all propagating degrees of freedom, whereas dynamical crossing introduces a regularity condition that governs consistent perturbative evolution—highlighting a crucial distinction between geometric embedding and temporal traversal of constraint singularities.

title: Revisiting the Axial Anomaly and Chiral Magnetic Effect in Dense Matter, with Applications to Axion Dark Matter
summary: We explicitly compute the axial anomaly in dense matter and show that its form remains unchanged from that in vacuum, even in the massless limit. This result follows from a subtle cancellation in the anomalous Ward identity between the medium-induced contributions to the divergence of the axial current and to the pseudoscalar density. We then revisit the chiral magnetic effect in a fermionic medium coupled to an axial chemical potential under an external magnetic field. We show that the medium supports a persistent, conserved anomalous current carried by fermions. The current is determined by the axial chemical potential and suppressed by the Fermi velocity, in agreement with anomalous axial-current correlation functions. We finally discuss applications to axion physics, where axion dark matter acts as an effective axial chemical potential.

AI.tldr: The paper computes the axial anomaly in dense matter, confirms its vacuum form persists even masslessly due to Ward identity cancellation, re-analyzes the chiral magnetic effect showing a persistent anomalous fermionic current determined by axial chemical potential and suppressed by Fermi velocity, and discusses implications for axion dark matter as an effective axial chemical potential.
AI.motivation: To resolve whether the axial anomaly—fundamental to quantum anomalies and topological effects—retains its vacuum form in dense fermionic media, and to clarify the nature of the chiral magnetic effect and its relevance to axion physics.
AI.method: Explicit computation of the axial anomaly in dense matter using the anomalous Ward identity; analysis of axial-current correlation functions; derivation of the chiral magnetic effect in presence of axial chemical potential and external magnetic field; interpretation of axion dark matter as an effective axial chemical potential.
AI.result: The axial anomaly retains its vacuum form in dense matter—even massless—due to exact cancellation between medium-induced contributions to axial current divergence and pseudoscalar density; a persistent, conserved anomalous current arises in the chiral magnetic effect, proportional to axial chemical potential and inversely proportional to Fermi velocity; axion dark matter induces an effective axial chemical potential enabling observable anomalous currents.
AI.conclusion: The axial anomaly is robust against medium effects, validating foundational assumptions in anomalous transport and axion phenomenology; the chiral magnetic effect in dense media yields a physically realizable, conserved anomalous current with direct implications for astrophysical and laboratory axion detection schemes.

title: Non-self-dual nontopological soliton in a pure Chern-Simons gauge model
summary: A nontopological soliton of the Q-ball type in a Chern-Simons-Higgs gauge model is studied using both analytical and numerical methods. The general non-self-dual case is considered. It is shown that the soliton solution is an extremum of the energy functional at a fixed Noether charge. A differential relation between the energy, Noether charge, and the boundary value of the gauge potential of the soliton is derived. A linear relation between the components of the soliton energy is obtained. The parametric domain of existence of the soliton solution is determined. It is established that the soliton properties depend significantly on the form of the self-interaction potential of the scalar field. In particular, the energy and charge of the soliton can take arbitrarily large values only if the self-interaction potential has two degenerate zero minima.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates nontopological Q-ball solitons in a Chern-Simons-Higgs model beyond the self-dual limit, deriving key energy–charge–gauge-potential relations, identifying existence conditions, and showing that unbounded energy/charge require a double-well scalar potential.
AI.motivation: To understand nontopological soliton (Q-ball) solutions in Chern-Simons-Higgs theory outside the restrictive self-dual regime, and to characterize their stability, energetics, and dependence on scalar self-interaction.
AI.method: Combined analytical variational analysis (extremization of energy at fixed Noether charge) and numerical computation; derivation of differential and linear energy relations; parametric domain mapping for solution existence.
AI.result: 1) Q-ball solution is an energy extremum at fixed Noether charge; 2) A differential relation linking energy, charge, and boundary gauge potential is derived; 3) A linear decomposition of soliton energy components is obtained; 4) Existence domain is explicitly determined; 5) Scalar potential structure dictates boundedness: only double-well (two degenerate minima) potentials allow arbitrarily large energy and charge.
AI.conclusion: Nontopological Q-balls in Chern-Simons-Higgs theory are robust beyond self-duality, but their physical viability—especially macroscopic charge/energy scaling—is critically governed by the scalar field’s self-interaction potential shape.

title: Statistical-Uncertainty-Driven Selection of Evaluation Frequency for Time-Dependent Sensing Calibration: A Demonstration with KAGRA Data
summary: Accurate calibration of the gravitational-wave strain h(t) is essential for both detection and astrophysical inference. In operating detectors, slow temporal variations in the sensing response are tracked using calibration lines, but practical constraints can prevent those lines from being injected at frequencies that are favorable for precise estimation of sensing-side parameters. We present a statistical framework for preselecting evaluation frequencies under such constraints. We apply this framework to KAGRA data from the first part of the fourth LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA Observing Run, for which the nominal cavity-pole frequency was about 18 Hz, while the sensing-side calibration line used in practice was injected at 32.7 Hz. For each candidate evaluation frequency, we construct the sensing function, quantify its segment-wise statistical uncertainty from empirical percentiles of the sample distribution, and rank the candidates using a score that combines the interval widths of the amplitude and phase. When a 1% amplitude interval width and a 1 degree phase interval width are weighted equally, 244 Hz is selected in all 4096 s analysis segments throughout the analyzed period. Relative to the reference frequency of 32.7 Hz, the amplitude interval width is reduced to about one quarter over a broad frequency range, while the phase interval width remains broadly comparable. We also assess the discrepancy introduced by frequency translation separately. These results suggest that the proposed method provides a useful statistical preselection framework for evaluation frequencies under practical operational constraints.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a statistical framework to preselect optimal evaluation frequencies for gravitational-wave strain calibration in detectors like KAGRA, improving amplitude uncertainty over broad bands while maintaining phase uncertainty—especially under constraints that prevent calibration line injection at ideal frequencies.
AI.motivation: Practical constraints in gravitational-wave detectors (e.g., KAGRA) limit calibration line injection to suboptimal frequencies (e.g., 32.7 Hz), hindering precise estimation of sensing-side parameters; the motivation is to statistically identify better evaluation frequencies despite such limitations.
AI.method: A statistical framework constructs the sensing function per candidate frequency, estimates segment-wise uncertainty via empirical percentiles of sample distributions, and ranks candidates using a composite score balancing amplitude (1% interval width) and phase (1° interval width) uncertainties.
AI.result: For KAGRA’s O4a data, 244 Hz was consistently selected across all 4096 s segments; amplitude uncertainty reduced to ~¼ of that at 32.7 Hz over a broad band, while phase uncertainty remained comparable; frequency-translation-induced discrepancy was separately quantified.
AI.conclusion: The proposed framework provides a robust, operationally feasible method for preselecting evaluation frequencies to enhance calibration precision under real-world constraints.

title: Evidence for New $D_s$-Family Molecular States
summary: Motivated by the observed $KD^{(*)}$ molecular candidates $D_{s0}(2317)$ and $D_{s1}(2460)$, their bottom--strange counterparts, $K\bar{B}^{(*)}$ molecular states, are naturally expected, although not yet experimentally established. This discrepancy may reflect sizable heavy-quark flavor symmetry breaking, which introduces significant model uncertainties.
