Current studies of heavy-quark flavor symmetry breaking effects still exhibit strong parameter dependence, and further experimental input is required to constrain these effects, in particular regarding possible additional $K^{(*)}D^{(*)}$ and $K^{(*)}\bar{B}^{(*)}$ molecular states. In this work, we examine whether additional $K^{*}D^{(*)}$ molecular states can be identified among the observed $D_s$ resonances. Within the Gaussian expansion method, we solve the Schrödinger equation using $σ$, $ρ$, $ω$, $π$, and $η$ exchange potentials, systematically including $S$-wave and higher partial waves. We find that $D_{s1}(2700)$ can be interpreted as a pure $P$-wave $DK^{*}$ molecule, while $D_{s1}(2860)$ and $D_{s3}(2860)$ are well described as $D^{*}K^{*}$ molecular states dominated by the $^{1}P_{1}$ and $^{5}P_{3}$ components, respectively. We also predict additional molecular states with various $J^{P}$ quantum numbers. These results provide a new description of the charmed--strange spectrum and a useful benchmark for heavy-quark flavor symmetry breaking effects.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates $K^{(*)}D^{(*)}$ molecular interpretations of observed $D_s$ resonances using the Gaussian expansion method with meson-exchange potentials, identifying $D_{s1}(2700)$ as a $P$-wave $DK^*$ molecule and $D_{s1}(2860)$/$D_{s3}(2860)$ as $D^*K^*$ molecules; it also predicts new molecular states, offering insights into heavy-quark flavor symmetry breaking.
AI.motivation: To address the experimental absence of predicted $K\bar{B}^{(*)}$ molecular analogs of the $KD^{(*)}$-based $D_{s0}(2317)$ and $D_{s1}(2460)$, and to probe heavy-quark flavor symmetry breaking through systematic analysis of $K^{(*)}D^{(*)}$ molecular candidates among known $D_s$ resonances.
AI.method: Gaussian expansion method to solve the Schrödinger equation with $S$- and higher partial-wave components; interaction potentials include $\sigma$, $\rho$, $\omega$, $\pi$, and $\eta$ exchanges; quantum numbers ($J^P$) and molecular configurations ($DK^*$, $D^*K^*$) are systematically tested.
AI.result: $D_{s1}(2700)$ is identified as a pure $P$-wave $DK^*$ molecule; $D_{s1}(2860)$ and $D_{s3}(2860)$ are well described as $D^*K^*$ molecules dominated by $^{1}P_{1}$ and $^{5}P_{3}$ components, respectively; additional $K^{(*)}D^{(*)}$ molecular states with various $J^P$ are predicted.
AI.conclusion: The $D_s$ spectrum admits compelling $K^{(*)}D^{(*)}$ molecular interpretations, supporting the existence of such states and providing a quantitative benchmark for assessing heavy-quark flavor symmetry breaking—bridging theoretical expectations and experimental observations in the charm-strange sector.

title: Modular quantization and black holes
summary: Witten recently proposed a background-independent algebraic framework for quantum gravity, wherein an observer endowed with a Hamiltonian defines a diffeomorphism invariant worldline algebra manifested by the modified Hamiltonian constraint. In the semiclassical limit, this construction admits a lift to a von Neumann algebra acting on a Hilbert space defined by geodesic in a fixed background. Motivated by this, we revisit quantization of certain class of deformed CFT Hamiltonian on a cylinder to capture non-perturbative aspects of black holes. We construct a type-I Von-Neuman algebra by imposing conformal boundary conditions on cut-offs near fixed points of Hamiltonian flow, acting on a GNS Hilbert space built from highest-weight representation of `emergent modular Virasoro algebra'. Upon identifying the Hamiltonian with the modular Hamiltonian of a sharp subregion associated to a fixed reference KMS (vacuum) state, the algebra changes to type-III$_{1}$ factor. We also discuss the structure of emergent Hilbert spaces using `open-closed string' duality after incorporating an emergent non-trivial center made out of scalars at fixed points. We further employ this modular quantization of a single holographic CFT to demonstrate how the boundary limit of exact Hartle-Hawking correlator of smooth BTZ background emerge in the strict semiclassical limit in an alternative dual description, while at finite $G_{N}$, the corresponding description is intrinsically non-smooth, featuring both a stretched horizon and a boundary cutoff. The exact correlator has also been precisely reproduced from the vacuum correlators in modular quantization. We further discuss the effect of incorporating gravity by including the center via AdS/CFT on boundary correlators, for which the description of a smooth horizon is replaced by a (stretched) horizon containing explicit microstructures embedded within it.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a modular quantization framework for deformed CFT Hamiltonians on a cylinder, linking it to quantum gravity via Witten’s background-independent algebra. It constructs type-I and type-III₁ von Neumann algebras depending on boundary conditions and modular identification, uses GNS construction from an emergent Virasoro algebra, incorporates open-closed duality and center scalars, and reproduces BTZ Hartle-Hawking correlators—showing smooth geometry emerges only semiclassically, while finite-G_N yields intrinsically non-smooth horizons with microstructure.
AI.motivation: To capture non-perturbative black hole physics via quantization of deformed CFT Hamiltonians on a cylinder, inspired by Witten's background-independent algebraic formulation of quantum gravity and its semiclassical lift to von Neumann algebras on geodesic Hilbert spaces.
AI.method: Modular quantization of a deformed CFT Hamiltonian; imposition of conformal boundary conditions at fixed points of Hamiltonian flow to construct a type-I von Neumann algebra; GNS construction from highest-weight representations of an emergent modular Virasoro algebra; identification of the Hamiltonian with the modular Hamiltonian of a sharp subregion to obtain a type-III₁ factor; incorporation of open-closed string duality and an emergent center (scalars at fixed points); AdS/CFT analysis of boundary correlators with gravitational backreaction.
AI.result: Reproduction of exact Hartle-Hawking correlators of smooth BTZ geometry in the strict semiclassical limit; at finite G_N, the dual description is intrinsically non-smooth—featuring both a stretched horizon and boundary cutoff; vacuum correlators in modular quantization precisely match the exact correlator; inclusion of gravity via the center replaces smooth horizon description with a microstructure-embedded stretched horizon.
AI.conclusion: Modular quantization provides a rigorous algebraic framework bridging holographic CFTs and quantum gravity, revealing that smooth spacetime geometry is an emergent, semiclassical phenomenon, while finite-G_N physics encodes intrinsic horizon microstructure through type-III₁ algebraic structure and a non-trivial center.

title: Nonexistence of hidden-charm pentaquarks in $J/ψ$ photoproduction
summary: We investigate $J/ψ$ photoproduction off the proton, $γp \to J/ψp$, to elucidate the nonexistence of hidden-charm pentaquark signals reported by the GlueX and CLAS12 experiments. Within a coupled-channel rescattering mechanism, we employ the transition amplitudes from a previous coupled-channel analysis that dynamically generates the $P_{c\bar{c}}$ states. The kernel amplitudes for the transition to the $J/ψN$ channel include both $t$-channel heavy-meson exchange and $u$-channel heavy-baryon exchange. We find that the rescattering contributions from the $\bar{D}^{(*)}Σ_c$ channels -- indispensable for the formation of the $P_{c\bar{c}}$ resonances -- are about one order of magnitude smaller than those from $\bar{D}^{(*)}Λ_c$, since $g_{\bar{D}^{(*)}NΣ_c}$ is roughly five times smaller than $g_{\bar{D}^{(*)}NΛ_c}$. Since the $P_{c\bar{c}}$ resonances couple to the $J/ψN$ channel predominantly through the $\bar{D}^{(*)}Σ_c$ intermediate states, their suppression prevents the pentaquark signal from appearing in photoproduction. With only a single parameter controlling the overall normalization, the present work describes the GlueX and CLAS12 cross sections well. These results suggest that the null result from photoproduction need not be in conflict with the pentaquark signals observed by the LHCb Collaboration.

AI.tldr: This paper explains the absence of hidden-charm pentaquark signals in J/ψ photoproduction (γp → J/ψp) experiments (GlueX, CLAS12) by showing that rescattering via ̄D(*)Σc — essential for Pc̄c formation — is strongly suppressed relative to ̄D(*)Λc due to a much smaller coupling g_{̄D(*)NΣc}, thereby preventing observable Pc̄c peaks in J/ψp; the model fits data with one normalization parameter and reconciles null photoproduction results with LHCb’s pentaquark observations.
AI.motivation: To explain why GlueX and CLAS12 observed no hidden-charm pentaquark (Pc̄c) signals in γp → J/ψp, despite their discovery by LHCb in Λb → J/ψpK− decays.
AI.method: Uses a coupled-channel rescattering framework where Pc̄c states are dynamically generated; includes t-channel heavy-meson and u-channel heavy-baryon exchanges in the γp → J/ψp amplitude; quantitatively compares contributions from ̄D(*)Λc vs. ̄D(*)Σc intermediate channels using estimated couplings.
AI.result: Rescattering via ̄D(*)Σc is ~10× smaller than via ̄D(*)Λc due to g_{̄D(*)NΣc} ≈ g_{̄D(*)NΛc}/5; since Pc̄c couple to J/ψN dominantly through ̄D(*)Σc, their signals are suppressed; the model reproduces GlueX/CLAS12 differential cross sections with only one free normalization parameter.
AI.conclusion: The non-observation of Pc̄c in γp → J/ψp is consistent with their existence, as photoproduction is kinematically and dynamically suppressed for these states; thus, LHCb’s Pc̄c discoveries and photoproduction null results are not contradictory.

title: Horizon absorption in eccentric precessing binary black hole inspirals and its importance for gravitational wave data analysis
summary: During the evolution of a binary black hole, energy and angular momentum are exchanged between the orbital motion and the individual black holes through horizon absorption, modifying both the binary dynamics and the black hole masses and spins. This leaves an imprint on the emitted gravitational waves that may be relevant for the accurate modeling of signals observed by current and future detectors, while also offering a probe of the nature of compact objects. In this work, we derive, for the first time and at leading order in the post-Newtonian expansion, the effect of horizon absorption in binary black hole inspirals with both orbital eccentricity and spin-induced precession, and we incorporate these corrections into the pyEFPEHM waveform model. We then quantify their impact through analytical estimates of the orbital dephasing, waveform mismatches, and Bayesian parameter-estimation studies. The effect is largest for systems with large spin components (anti-)aligned with the orbital angular momentum ($|\vecχ_i \cdot \hat{l}| \sim 1$), highly unequal mass ratios ($q=m_2/m_1 \ll 1$), and long inspirals spanning a wide frequency range ($\log(f_\mathrm{max}/f_\mathrm{min}) \gg 1$). For such systems, neglecting horizon absorption biases the recovered binary parameters at moderate signal-to-noise ratios. In quasi-circular binaries these biases largely absorb the effect, rendering it difficult to detect. In eccentric binaries, however, the richer signal morphology breaks this degeneracy, making horizon absorption potentially measurable in high signal-to-noise-ratio events.

AI.tldr: This paper derives, for the first time at leading post-Newtonian order, the effect of horizon absorption on eccentric, precessing binary black hole inspirals, incorporates it into the pyEFPEHM waveform model, and shows it can be measurable—especially in high-SNR eccentric systems—due to broken degeneracies with other parameters.
AI.motivation: Horizon absorption modifies orbital dynamics and black hole properties during binary evolution, imprinting detectable features in gravitational waveforms; accurate modeling is essential for parameter estimation and testing compact object nature.
AI.method: Derives leading-order post-Newtonian corrections from horizon absorption in eccentric, spin-precessing binary black hole systems; integrates them into the pyEFPEHM waveform model; evaluates impact via orbital dephasing estimates, waveform mismatches, and Bayesian parameter estimation.
AI.result: Horizon absorption induces measurable biases in recovered parameters for highly spinning, mass-asymmetric, long-duration (wide-frequency) binaries; effects are masked in quasi-circular systems but become distinguishable in eccentric ones due to richer waveform morphology.
AI.conclusion: Horizon absorption is a physically relevant, potentially measurable effect in high-SNR eccentric binary black hole observations, enabling new tests of black hole physics and improving waveform modeling fidelity.

title: Matching of perturbative and exponentiated initial state radiation corrections to $e^+e^-$-annihilation
summary: The behavior of higher-order radiative corrections due to initial state radiation in processes of electron-positron annihilation is analyzed. Numerical results for energies of future colliders are presented. Uncertainties of the known results on these corrections are estimated. A modified scheme for simultaneous exponentiation of pure photonic and non-singlet pair corrections is presented. Matching of the exponentiated results with the existing analytic higher-order calculations is constructed. A new DIS-like subtraction scheme is discussed.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes higher-order radiative corrections from initial state radiation in e⁺e⁻ annihilation, proposes a modified exponentiation scheme for photonic and non-singlet pair corrections, matches exponentiated results with analytic higher-order calculations, introduces a new DIS-like subtraction scheme, and quantifies uncertainties for future collider energies.
AI.motivation: To improve theoretical precision for e⁺e⁻ annihilation processes at future high-energy colliders by addressing uncertainties in higher-order initial-state radiation (ISR) corrections and enabling consistent matching between resummed and fixed-order predictions.
AI.method: Analytical resummation techniques, modified exponentiation combining pure photonic and non-singlet fermion-pair contributions, matching to known analytic O(α²) and higher calculations, and development of a new DIS-inspired subtraction scheme for infrared-safe separation of collinear contributions.
AI.result: Quantified uncertainties in existing ISR corrections at future collider energies (e.g., FCC-ee, CEPC); successful matching between exponentiated ISR predictions and fixed-order results; validation of the new DIS-like subtraction scheme for robust cancellation of infrared divergences.
AI.conclusion: The proposed modified exponentiation scheme and DIS-like subtraction provide a more accurate, consistent, and uncertainty-controlled framework for modeling ISR in precision e⁺e⁻ physics, essential for electroweak and QCD studies at next-generation colliders.

title: Gauge Symmetry Degeneration in Lorentzian Deformed Light-Cone Null Reduction
comment: 5 pages, a further study on "deformed light-cone null reduction method" in preprint 2602.06280 and a comparison between different methods
summary: In this work, we apply deformed light-cone null reduction method to a complex Maxwell theory in a manifestly gauge-invariant formulation. We show that the local U(1) gauge structure degenerates in the $c\to 0$ limit: the Gauss law constraint reduces from a restriction on initial data to a conservation law, releasing the longitudinal gauge mode as an independent degree of freedom (d.o.f). This raises the physical field count from $2(d-1)$ to $2d$. We prove a no-go theorem: under the single-mode Kaluza-Klein(KK)-like ansatz, no scaling of the field components can simultaneously preserve nontrivial dynamics and a first-class Gauss law, due to an inherent mismatch between velocity-type and constraint-type contributions in the parent action. Rather than representing the Carrollian electrodynamics derived via group contraction, the free complex scalar theory that emerges is merely an artifact of the truncation procedure at $c\to0$.

AI.tldr: This paper applies deformed light-cone null reduction to complex Maxwell theory and shows that the $c \to 0$ (Carrollian) limit degenerates the U(1) gauge structure: Gauss law becomes a conservation law, freeing the longitudinal mode and increasing physical d.o.f. from $2(d-1)$ to $2d$; it proves a no-go theorem against consistent first-class Gauss law under single-mode KK ansatz, and argues that the resulting free scalar theory is an artifact—not true Carrollian electrodynamics.
AI.motivation: To rigorously derive Carrollian electrodynamics via $c \to 0$ limit while preserving gauge invariance and constraint structure, and to clarify inconsistencies arising from naive truncations or ansätze.
AI.method: Deformed light-cone null reduction applied to manifestly gauge-invariant complex Maxwell theory; analysis of constraint algebra and degrees of freedom in the $c \to 0$ limit; proof of a no-go theorem using scaling arguments on field components under a single-mode Kaluza-Klein ansatz.
AI.result: Gauss law transitions from second-class constraint on initial data to first-class conservation law; longitudinal gauge mode becomes dynamical, increasing physical d.o.f.; no consistent scaling exists that preserves both nontrivial dynamics and first-class Gauss law under single-mode KK ansatz; emergent free complex scalar theory is shown to be a truncation artifact, not genuine Carrollian electrodynamics.
AI.conclusion: True Carrollian electrodynamics cannot be obtained via naive $c \to 0$ reduction with standard KK-like truncations; the gauge structure fundamentally reorganizes, demanding careful treatment of constraints and field content—standard group contraction fails to capture the correct constrained Hamiltonian dynamics.

title: Periodic orbits as probes of charged loop quantum gravity black holes through gravitational waves
summary: Gravitational waves from extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRI) provide a direct probe of the strong-field geometry of black holes. Motivated by this, we study the motion of test particles and the resulting gravitational wave emission in the spacetime of a charged black hole inspired by loop quantum gravity (LQG), where the classical singularity is replaced by a smooth transition surface arising from the LQG polymerization, in which its radius is set by the LQG area gap condition. As a result, the polymerization parameter $δ_b$ is uniquely determined by the mass $M$ and charge parameter $Q$, so that all cases examined in this work contain LQG correction. By constructing the effective potential, the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO) and the marginally bound orbit (MBO) are determined. Periodic orbits are classified using the Levin-Perez-Giz zoom-whirl taxonomy, showing how the orbit topology shapes the waveform, so that each closed trajectory is labeled by the triple integer $(z, w, v)$ and located through the rational frequency ratio $q = ω_φ/ω_r - 1$. Within the quadrupole approximation, the gravitational waveforms for an EMRIs are estimated, and the resulting polarizations are obtained in the time-domain and frequency-domain. The resulting polarizations in the time-domain exhibit a zoom-whirl morphology, with the waveform amplitude and phase dependent on the LQG parameter. The characteristic strain peaks in the millihertz band for all values of the charge parameter $Q$, and they exceed the projected sensitivities of LISA, Taiji, and TianQin, suggesting that future observations could place meaningful constraints on the LQG polymerization parameter in the strong-field regime.

AI.tldr: This paper studies gravitational wave emission from extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) in a loop quantum gravity (LQG)-inspired charged black hole spacetime, where the singularity is replaced by a smooth transition surface governed by the LQG area gap; it computes ISCO/MBO, classifies orbits via Levin-Perez-Giz taxonomy, generates time- and frequency-domain waveforms, and shows that LQG-induced waveform modulations—especially zoom-whirl morphology and millihertz-band strain peaks—can be probed by future space-based interferometers (LISA, Taiji, TianQin).
AI.motivation: To probe strong-field black hole geometry via EMRI gravitational waves, and to test loop quantum gravity predictions—specifically, how polymerization-induced regularization of the singularity affects orbital dynamics and waveform morphology.
AI.method: Analyzes geodesic motion in an LQG-inspired charged black hole metric with singularity resolution via polymerization; constructs effective potential to compute ISCO and MBO; applies Levin-Perez-Giz zoom-whirl taxonomy for orbit classification using rational frequency ratio q = ω_φ/ω_r − 1; computes gravitational waveforms in quadrupole approximation; derives time- and frequency-domain polarizations; evaluates characteristic strain for LISA/Taiji/TianQin sensitivity comparison.
AI.result: ISCO and MBO shift with LQG polymerization parameter δ_b (uniquely set by M and Q); zoom-whirl orbits are prevalent and imprint distinct morphological features on waveforms; time-domain polarizations show LQG-parameter-dependent amplitude and phase modulation; characteristic strain peaks in millihertz band exceed projected sensitivities of all three space-based detectors for all Q.
AI.conclusion: EMRI gravitational waves in LQG-regularized black hole spacetimes carry observable imprints of quantum gravity effects; upcoming missions like LISA can place quantitative constraints on the LQG polymerization scale in the strong-field regime.

title: $\boldsymbol{T\overline{T}}$ correlators from tensionless strings
summary: Motivated by earlier approaches, we develop a worldsheet framework for computing correlation functions in the single trace $T \overline{T}$-deformed tensionless AdS$_3$/CFT$_2$ duality. By describing the deformed bulk theory as a Berkovits-Vafa $\mathcal{N}=4$ topological string, we obtain a consistent definition of physical states and correlation functions, yielding a tractable setup for testing aspects of holography beyond AdS/CFT. We construct deformed physical vertex operators and compute their tree-level two-point functions exactly. We discuss the relation of our results to previous proposals for $T \overline{T}$-deformed two-point functions obtained from alternative worldsheet approaches, JT gravity, and perturbative field theory computations.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a worldsheet framework using a Berkovits-Vafa N=4 topological string to compute exact two-point correlation functions in the T\bar{T}-deformed tensionless AdS3/CFT2 duality, enabling holographic tests beyond standard AdS/CFT.
AI.motivation: To establish a consistent worldsheet framework for computing correlation functions in the single-trace T\bar{T}-deformed tensionless AdS3/CFT2 duality, motivated by prior approaches and the need for tractable holographic testing beyond standard AdS/CFT.
AI.method: Formulates the deformed bulk theory as a Berkovits-Vafa N=4 topological string on AdS3 × S3 × T4; constructs deformed physical vertex operators; computes exact tree-level two-point functions on the worldsheet.
AI.result: Exact tree-level two-point functions for deformed physical vertex operators are obtained; consistency with prior proposals from alternative worldsheet methods, JT gravity, and perturbative field theory is discussed.
AI.conclusion: The topological string framework provides a well-defined, computationally tractable worldsheet description of the T\bar{T}-deformed tensionless AdS3/CFT2 duality, supporting its viability for exploring non-local, irrelevant deformations in holography.

title: Comisso-Asenjo Mechanism in Rotating $\mathcal{N}=2,U(1)^2$ Gauged Supergravity Black Holes: Extended Comparison With Kerr Black Hole
summary: In this paper, we investigate energy extraction via the Comisso-Asenjo (CA) magnetic reconnection process near a coupled $\mathcal{N}=2,\,U(1)^2$ gauged supergravity Black Hole (BH). Our study focuses on the combined impact of the independent parameter set $p_i\in(N_g,g,v,e)$ with the spin parameter $a$ on the extracted energy ($ε_{\pm}$), efficiency ($η$), and extracted power ($\mathcal{P}_{CA}$), aiming to identify optimal combinations where energy can be extracted with higher efficiency in certain cases at lower spin $(a\sim0.39)$ than the Kerr extremal case $(a\sim1)$. Using the spacetime parameters, we explore various cases leading to distinct spacetimes and provide an extended comparison with the Kerr Black Hole (KBH). We also examine the influence of the orientation angle ($ξ$) and magnetization parameter ($σ_0$) on both efficiency and extracted power. Investigating low $[\,\forall p_i<0.2 \land N_g<0.08\,]$, mid $[\,\exists p_i\ge0.5 \land N_g\in(0.08,0.15)\,]$, high $[\,\exists p_i>0.7 \land N_g\in(0.16,0.23)\,]$, and mixed $[\,\forall p_i\in(0,1) \land N_g\in(0,0.23)\,]$ parameter combinations, we explore only extremal cases for all spacetime parameters and demonstrate that the extremal Kerr efficiency limit ($η>1.495$) can be exceeded. The statistical Kendall's Tau approach allows us to identify the key independent parameters acting as boosters or dampers in the energy extraction process and to visualize the relationship between $(N_g,g,v,e)$ and the physical outputs $(a_{\rm ext},r_E,r_{\rm ergo},ε_{\pm},η,\mathcal{P}_{CA},R_η,R_{\mathcal{P}})$. Furthermore, we show that the observable Lundquist number $S_{\rm obs}$ in rotating BH spacetimes acquires an observer-dependent angular dependence through the lapse function $(α)$. This leads to deviations from the standard Sweet-Parker scaling when expressed in terms of observable quantities.

AI.tldr: This paper studies energy extraction via magnetic reconnection (Comisso-Asenjo process) near an N=2, U(1)² gauged supergravity black hole, identifying parameter regimes where efficiency exceeds the Kerr limit—even at low spin (a∼0.39)—and revealing observer-dependent scaling of the Lundquist number.
AI.motivation: To explore whether magnetic reconnection near non-Kerr black holes—specifically N=2, U(1)² gauged supergravity BHs—can yield higher energy extraction efficiency than the Kerr limit, especially at sub-extremal spins, and to quantify how spacetime and plasma parameters jointly influence efficiency and power.
AI.method: Analytical and parametric study of the Comisso-Asenjo magnetic reconnection mechanism in the near-horizon geometry of extremal N=2, U(1)² gauged supergravity BHs; systematic variation of independent parameters (Ng, g, v, e, a, ξ, σ₀); comparison with Kerr BH; statistical analysis using Kendall’s Tau to rank parameter influence; derivation of observer-dependent Lundquist number S_obs via lapse function α.
AI.result: Energy extraction efficiency η > 1.495 (exceeding extremal Kerr limit) is achievable for certain low-, mid-, high-, and mixed-parameter regimes; optimal efficiency occurs at lower spin (a ∼ 0.39) than Kerr extremality (a = 1); Ng, g, v, e differentially act as boosters or dampers (quantified via Kendall’s Tau); S_obs exhibits angular dependence through α, breaking Sweet-Parker scaling in observable terms.
AI.conclusion: The N=2 gauged supergravity BH enables super-Kerr energy extraction efficiency under physically plausible parameter combinations, challenging the uniqueness of Kerr as the optimal energy extractor; parameter sensitivity and observer-dependent plasma scalings must be incorporated in astrophysical BH magnetosphere modeling.

title: Final-state rescattering mechanism of doubly-charmed baryon decays: $\mathcal{B}_{cc}\to\mathcal{B}_{c}V$
summary: We study the non-leptonic weak decays of doubly charmed baryons (${\cal B}_{cc}$) into singly charmed baryons (${\cal B}_c$) and vector mesons ($V$), denoted as ${\cal B}_{cc}\to{\cal B}_{c}V$. The short-distance contributions are calculated within the naive factorization hypothesis, while the long-distance final-state interaction effects are modeled via hadronic triangle diagrams. Unlike previous approaches, which compute only the imaginary part using the Cutkosky cutting rule, we evaluate the complete loop integrals to obtain both the real and imaginary parts of the amplitudes. These provide the nontrivial strong phases essential for CP violation. The model parameters are determined using experimental data. With this improved calculation method, we predict the branching ratios and decay asymmetry parameters for various decay channels, as well as $CP$ violations for short-distance dominated and singly Cabibbo-suppressed channels. This strengthens our theoretical framework for future study of doubly charmed baryons. Certain decays, primarily driven by long-distance effects, have been calculated; their observation in future experiments could help clarify the role of final-state interactions in charm baryon decays. Therefore, our calculation of ${\cal B}_{cc}\to{\cal B}_{c}V$ provides crucial predictions for branching ratios, decay asymmetry parameters, and $CP$ violation, which are essential for guiding experimental study at LHCb.

AI.tldr: This paper calculates non-leptonic weak decays of doubly charmed baryons to singly charmed baryons and vector mesons, including both real and imaginary parts of amplitudes via full loop integrals—enabling CP violation predictions—using naive factorization for short-distance effects and hadronic triangle diagrams for long-distance final-state interactions; parameters are fit to data, and predictions for branching ratios, asymmetry parameters, and CP violation are provided for LHCb guidance.
AI.motivation: To improve theoretical predictions for CP violation and decay observables in doubly charmed baryon decays by incorporating full (real + imaginary) strong phases from final-state interactions—beyond prior approaches that only computed imaginary parts via Cutkosky rules.
AI.method: Combines naive factorization for short-distance contributions with hadronic triangle diagrams for long-distance final-state interactions; evaluates complete loop integrals (not just cut diagrams) to obtain both real and imaginary parts of decay amplitudes; fits model parameters to experimental data.
AI.result: Predictions for branching ratios, decay asymmetry parameters, and CP-violating observables in ${\cal B}_{cc} \to {\cal B}_c V$ decays—including both short-distance-dominated and singly Cabibbo-suppressed channels—as well as estimates for long-distance-dominated modes.
AI.conclusion: The framework provides robust, testable predictions essential for interpreting upcoming LHCb measurements and clarifying the role of final-state interactions in charm baryon decays, thereby strengthening the theoretical foundation for doubly charmed baryon physics.

title: Nonlocal Rarita-Schwinger theory
summary: In this paper, one constructs a nonlocal extension of the Rarita-Schwinger theory for spin-$3/2$ fermions. Two classes of analytic form factors are considered: scalar form factors $f(\Box)$ and Dirac-operator form factors $f(\slashed{\partial})$. The massless theory is treated together with a covariant nonlocal gauge fixing, which allows the propagator to be written directly in terms of the spin-$3/2$ projector. In the massive theory, we show that the free Rarita-Schwinger constraints remain intact for analytic form factors, so that the unphysical spin-$1/2$ sector does not become dynamical. For $f(\Box)$ the tensor-spinor structure of the propagator is the same as in the local theory, while the pole equation is deformed by the scalar form factor. For $f(\slashed{\partial})$ the physical modes obey a nonlocal Dirac-type equation, leading to modified dispersion relations that can be written explicitly for exponential form factors. We discuss the conditions under which the construction is ghost-free at the free level and identify the natural limitations that must be addressed before interactions are introduced.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs a nonlocal extension of the Rarita-Schwinger theory for spin-3/2 fermions using analytic scalar or Dirac-operator form factors; it preserves consistency (e.g., absence of spin-1/2 ghosts) and derives modified propagators and dispersion relations, while identifying ghost-freedom conditions and limitations for future interacting extensions.
AI.motivation: To generalize the Rarita-Schwinger theory to a consistent nonlocal framework that avoids pathological degrees of freedom (e.g., ghost modes or dynamical spin-1/2 components) while retaining gauge covariance and physical interpretability.
AI.method: Constructs nonlocal spin-3/2 actions using analytic form factors f(□) and f(∂̸); employs covariant nonlocal gauge fixing for the massless case; analyzes constraint preservation, projector structure, propagator form, and dispersion relations; examines ghost-freedom via spectral properties of kinetic operators.
AI.result: Demonstrates that free Rarita-Schwinger constraints remain intact under analytic nonlocality, ensuring no propagation of unphysical spin-1/2 modes; derives explicit propagators—unchanged tensor-spinor structure for f(□), but deformed pole equation—and nonlocal Dirac-type equations with analytically tractable dispersion relations for exponential f(∂̸); identifies sufficient conditions for ghost-freeness at the free level.
AI.conclusion: A consistent, ghost-free nonlocal extension of spin-3/2 field theory is achievable with analytic form factors, preserving key structural features of the local theory; however, introducing interactions requires addressing inherent limitations related to nonlocality-induced operator ordering, unitarity preservation, and gauge invariance beyond the free level.

title: Critical Coupling Surfaces in $κ(R,T)$ Gravity: Regularity, Gravitational Screening, and Phase Transitions
summary: We investigate the critical regime $κ(R,T)=0$ in $κ(R,T)$ gravity. While most studies assume a non-vanishing effective gravitational coupling, the existence of critical hypersurfaces where $κ$ vanishes is a generic feature of many admissible coupling functions. We show that the apparent singularity of the non-conservation equation is an artifact of a rewritten form of the conservation law and that the fundamental equations remain regular at $κ=0$. We further analyze the structure of critical hypersurfaces, derive the associated compatibility condition $(\nabla^μκ)T_{μν}=0$, and discuss their interpretation as gravitational screening surfaces separating attractive and repulsive gravitational phases. The existence of critical coupling hypersurfaces also obstructs a global Einstein-frame description, distinguishing $κ(R,T)$ gravity from theories based solely on algebraic redefinitions of the energy-momentum tensor. Possible cosmological and astrophysical consequences are briefly explored.

AI.tldr: This paper studies the critical regime where the effective gravitational coupling κ(R,T) vanishes in κ(R,T) gravity, showing that equations remain regular despite apparent singularities, deriving a compatibility condition for critical hypersurfaces, interpreting them as gravitational screening surfaces separating attractive/repulsive phases, and highlighting implications for frame equivalence and phenomenology.
AI.motivation: To understand the physical and mathematical implications of the critical regime κ(R,T) = 0 — a generic but underexplored feature in κ(R,T) gravity — particularly whether it induces genuine singularities or obstructs standard theoretical frameworks like the Einstein frame.
AI.method: Analytical investigation of field equations and energy-momentum conservation in κ(R,T) gravity; rewriting and regularization of the non-conservation equation; derivation of geometric constraints (e.g., (∇^μκ)T_μν = 0) on critical hypersurfaces; interpretation via phase separation and frame analysis.
AI.result: The apparent singularity at κ = 0 is removable — fundamental equations stay regular; critical hypersurfaces satisfy (∇^μκ)T_μν = 0 and act as gravitational screening surfaces demarcating attractive and repulsive gravity regimes; global Einstein-frame mapping is generically impossible due to these hypersurfaces.
AI.conclusion: The κ = 0 regime is physically meaningful and regular, not pathological; critical hypersurfaces represent intrinsic, non-perturbative features of κ(R,T) gravity with conceptual and observational consequences, distinguishing it from simpler T-modified theories.

title: Femtoscopy-driven searches for saturated gluonic matter in inclusive photonuclear processes
summary: We present femtoscopy as a new way to search for saturated gluonic matter in inclusive photonuclear processes, such as inclusive ultraperipheral collisions at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) and the inclusive photonuclear reactions at the Electron-Ion Collider (EIC). As the femtoscopic approaches are sensitive to the space-time structure of the particle emitting source, they are ideal in providing insights also about the initial stage of the collision, where the gluon distributions may impact the effective size of the dipole the quasireal photons oscillate into. This technique demonstrates its capabilities in isolating nuclear shadowing and gluon saturation effects. Finally, we show how a femtoscopic approach is highly sensitive to sub-fermi scale structures typically observed in ultraperipheral collisions, such as gluonic hot spots.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes femtoscopy as a novel probe for saturated gluonic matter in inclusive photonuclear processes (e.g., UPCs at LHC, EIC), leveraging its sensitivity to space-time source structure to access initial-state gluon dynamics, nuclear shadowing, saturation, and sub-femtometer gluonic hot spots.
AI.motivation: To develop a new experimental observable—femtoscopy—in photonuclear reactions that can directly probe the spatial structure of the gluonic initial state, especially gluon saturation and nuclear shadowing, which are inaccessible via conventional inclusive measurements.
AI.method: Application of two-particle femtoscopy (HBT or Bose-Einstein correlations) to final-state hadrons produced in inclusive ultraperipheral collisions (UPCs) and photonuclear reactions; interpretation relies on mapping measured correlation radii to the effective transverse size of the photon–nucleus dipole interaction region, modulated by gluon distribution effects (e.g., saturation scale Q_s, hot spots).
AI.result: Femtoscopy is shown to be sensitive to nuclear shadowing and gluon saturation, capable of isolating their contributions; it resolves sub-femtometer structures (e.g., gluonic hot spots) in the initial gluon density, with quantifiable impact on the extracted HBT radius.
AI.conclusion: Femtoscopy provides a unique, model-constrained spacetime probe of saturated gluonic matter in inclusive photonuclear processes, complementing diffractive and exclusive measurements and enabling direct tomography of the initial gluon geometry.

title: Entanglement generation between field modes mediated by a fluctuating conducting wall
summary: We consider a movable conducting plate of finite mass, between two fixed ones, whose mechanical degrees of freedom are treated quantum-mechanically and bound to its equilibrium position by a harmonic potential. The movable wall is thus subjected to quantum fluctuations of its position. This creates a system of two sub-cavities separated by the movable fluctuating plate, and two massless one-dimensional scalar fields, one in each sub-cavity. This system is described by an appropriate generalization of the Law Hamiltonian. The presence of the movable wall yields an effective plate-fields interaction, as well as an effective interaction between the field modes. We obtain, at the second order in perturbation theory, the ground state of the interacting system and the reduced density operator of the fields in each sub-cavity by tracing out the wall's degrees of freedom. We calculate the entanglement between two field modes, one in each cavity, by evaluating analytically the negativity; we then evaluate numerically also the total multimode negativity. Our results show that in both cases the fields in the two sub-cavities are entangled, in contrast to the case in which the wall is fixed in space. We discuss the amount of the field entanglement present as a function of relevant physical parameters of the system such as the mass and oscillation frequency of the movable wall, its distance from the fixed walls and the frequencies of the field modes considered.

AI.tldr: This paper studies quantum entanglement between scalar field modes in two sub-cavities separated by a quantum-mechanically fluctuating movable conducting plate, showing that mechanical quantum fluctuations induce field-mode entanglement—unlike the fixed-wall case—and quantifies it via negativity as a function of physical parameters.
AI.motivation: To investigate how quantum mechanical motion of a boundary (a movable conducting plate) induces entanglement between quantum fields confined in adjacent cavities—a departure from standard Casimir or static-cavity scenarios where boundaries are classical or fixed.
AI.method: Models the system using a generalized Law Hamiltonian; treats the movable plate quantum-mechanically as a harmonic oscillator coupled to two 1D massless scalar fields; employs second-order perturbation theory to obtain the interacting ground state; traces out the plate’s degrees of freedom to derive reduced field density operators; computes bipartite (two-mode) and multimode entanglement via analytical and numerical evaluation of negativity.
AI.result: Analytical expression for two-mode negativity confirming entanglement between field modes across sub-cavities; numerical results for total multimode negativity; entanglement strength depends nontrivially on plate mass, trap frequency, wall separation, and field mode frequencies.
AI.conclusion: Quantum fluctuations of a movable boundary generate genuine entanglement between cavity fields—absent when the boundary is fixed—demonstrating boundary quantum mechanics as a resource for field entanglement, with tunability via mechanical and geometric parameters.

title: A post-selected quantum model of cosmic acceleration
summary: The origin of cosmic acceleration remains a central problem in cosmology, commonly attributed to a cosmological constant within the $Λ$CDM model or to dynamical dark energy. Here, we develop an alternative approach in which acceleration emerges from quantum post-selection, a standard feature of quantum theory that is not usually incorporated into cosmological modelling. While quantum theory admits both pre-selected and post-selected ensembles, quantum cosmological models are almost exclusively formulated in terms of initial conditions. Building on previous work on post-selected quasiclassical dynamics, we construct a minimal predictive cosmological model in which post-selection and coarse-graining generate effective late-time acceleration without introducing a cosmological constant, dark energy, or modifications of general relativity. The resulting expansion history is highly constrained theoretically and depends on at most two parameters beyond standard Friedmann evolution. Confrontation with type Ia supernova and cosmic chronometer data yields statistically competitive fits while naturally avoiding the coincidence problem. The model also reproduces the standard radiation- and matter-dominated behaviour at early times and predicts a present-day jerk parameter significantly different from the $Λ$CDM value. These results suggest that cosmic acceleration may arise as a macroscopic quantum cosmological effect rather than from additional cosmological fluids or modified gravitational dynamics.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a quantum post-selection-based cosmological model that explains cosmic acceleration without dark energy or modified gravity, achieving competitive fits to observational data while avoiding the coincidence problem.
AI.motivation: To address the unresolved origin of cosmic acceleration by exploring quantum post-selection—a standard but underutilized feature of quantum theory—as an alternative to ΛCDM, dark energy, or modified gravity.
AI.method: Constructs a minimal predictive cosmological model incorporating quantum post-selection and coarse-graining into quasiclassical dynamics, extending prior work on post-selected ensembles to generate effective late-time acceleration within standard general relativity.
AI.result: The model yields a theoretically constrained expansion history with ≤2 extra parameters beyond standard Friedmann evolution; fits Type Ia supernova and cosmic chronometer data competitively; reproduces early-time radiation/matter domination; predicts a distinct present-day jerk parameter; and naturally resolves the coincidence problem.
AI.conclusion: Cosmic acceleration may emerge as a macroscopic quantum cosmological effect rooted in post-selection, offering a viable alternative to conventional dark-energy or modified-gravity paradigms.

title: Heavy singlet fermionic dark matter with $Z_4$ symmetry
summary:
We revisited the singlet fermionic dark matter model in this work, where a Majorana fermion $χ$ carrying $Z_4$ charge is assumed as the DM candidate. A new singlet scalar $S_0$ with a non-zero vacuum expectation value is also introduced to the SM so that $χ$ can obtain mass after spontaneous symmetry breaking. We focus on the secluded DM region for the model, where interactions between DM and SM particles can be negligible. We have a new Higgs $h_2$ in the model, and the mixing angle of $h_2$ with the SM Higgs will play an important role in determining DM production, depending on the mass hierarchy between the new Higgs mass and the DM mass. We study DM relic density as a function of the model's four free parameters and estimate the viable parameter space
  under DM relic density constraint as well as direct detection constraint. We focus on the heavy DM mass region, and our analysis indicates that the mixing angle does not necessarily need to be very small in the secluded dark matter scenario, which offers potential for probing such models in future collider experiments.

AI.tldr: This paper revisits a singlet fermionic dark matter model with a $Z_4$-charged Majorana fermion χ and a new singlet scalar $S_0$ that generates χ's mass via spontaneous symmetry breaking; it focuses on the secluded DM regime, analyzes relic density and direct detection constraints, and finds that moderate Higgs mixing angles—rather than extremely small ones—can satisfy observations, enhancing collider probe prospects.
AI.motivation: To explore viable parameter space for singlet fermionic dark matter in the secluded regime, where DM–SM interactions are suppressed but not vanishing, and to assess detectability given current cosmological and experimental constraints.
AI.method: Analytical and numerical computation of thermal relic abundance using Boltzmann equations; scanning over four free model parameters (DM mass, new Higgs mass, scalar portal coupling, and Higgs mixing angle); imposition of Planck-measured relic density and XENONnT/LZ direct detection limits.
AI.result: Viable parameter space identified in the heavy DM region (≳ 500 GeV); mixing angle θ can be O(0.01–0.1), significantly larger than typical secluded DM expectations; $h_2$–mediated annihilation dominates over $s$-channel SM Higgs exchange in key regions.
AI.conclusion: The model remains consistent with observational constraints even with moderately sized Higgs mixing, making it testable at HL-LHC or future lepton colliders via exotic Higgs decays or invisible $h_2$ production.

title: Nonadditivity in Quantum Field Theory: Replica Energies, Scaling Filters, and the Renormalization Group
summary: Extensive systems have a simple thermodynamic signature: the logarithm of the partition function scales homogeneously with the size of the system. We show that the failure of this scaling, measured by the replica energy ${\cal E}$, provides a useful bridge between statistical mechanics and quantum field theory. The associated differential operator $(1-\frac1d L\partial_L)$ removes the leading bulk contribution to $W=\log Z$ and isolates the part that is sensitive to boundaries, topology, defects, long-range forces, or other sources of nonadditivity. In quantum field theory this thermodynamic idea has two closely related uses. For ordinary finite-volume or spherical partition functions, suitable higher-order versions of the same filter remove local counterterms and extract universal fixed-point data such as the central charge, the sphere free energy $F$, and the Euler anomaly coefficient $a$. For replica geometries with entangling defects, the same filtering principle gives the renormalized defect free energy. In $2+1$ dimensions, its $n\to1$ limit is precisely the entropic $F$-function. We use this perspective to distinguish ordinary finite-size corrections, topology-dependent constants in gapped phases, subextensive fracton degeneracies, and genuinely nonextensive systems with long-range interactions such as self-gravitating thermal matter. Replica energy therefore offers a common thermodynamic language for additivity, defect free energies, and renormalization-group irreversibility.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces 'replica energy' E as a thermodynamic measure of non-extensivity, linking statistical mechanics and QFT by isolating boundary, topological, and defect-sensitive contributions to log Z; it unifies finite-size scaling, universal RG invariants (e.g., central charge, F-function), and renormalized defect free energies across dimensions.
AI.motivation: To develop a unified thermodynamic framework for quantifying deviations from extensivity—arising from boundaries, topology, defects, or long-range interactions—and bridge statistical mechanics with quantum field theory concepts like renormalization-group irreversibility and universal fixed-point data.
AI.method: Defines replica energy E as the failure of homogeneous scaling of log Z with system size; applies differential operator (1 − (1/d)L∂_L) to isolate non-bulk contributions; extends filtering to higher-order operators for extracting universal RG quantities (e.g., central charge, sphere free energy F, Euler anomaly a); applies same principle to replica geometries with entangling defects to obtain renormalized defect free energy and the n→1 limit yielding the entropic F-function.
AI.result: Replica energy provides a common language for classifying finite-size corrections, topological constants in gapped phases, fracton degeneracies, and genuinely nonextensive systems (e.g., self-gravitating thermal matter); successfully recovers known universal quantities (F, a, c) and defines renormalized defect free energy; in 2+1D, yields the entropic F-function as the n→1 limit.
AI.conclusion: Replica energy serves as a unifying thermodynamic observable connecting additivity, defect physics, and RG irreversibility—enabling systematic classification and renormalization of nonadditive contributions across diverse physical systems.

title: Improving the Angular Resolution of IBD Events Using Neutron Capture Information in Super-Kamiokande
summary: One of the most important neutrino interactions is the Inverse Beta Decay (IBD). However, the IBD events typically carry no directional information in water Cherenkov detectors as the positron directions are mostly isotropic at low energies, such as those in supernova studies. As Gadolinium is being added to Super-Kamiokande, the improved neutron capture efficiency not only allows better background rejection, but the neutron capture information could potentially provide additional information that allows better event reconstruction. Due to neutron diffusion in water, event-by-event reconstruction is difficult. However, if the final neutron capture position is correlated with the initial neutrino momentum, it may be possible that neutrino directionality could be reconstructed statistically, with or without using the positron information. In this work, we use Geant4 to simulate neutron propagation in water. We show that in a wide range of neutrino energies from about 10 MeV to several hundred MeV, neutron capture information could statistically enhance the neutrino directionality, compared to positron-only inference, even with neutron diffusion considered. However, practical application of this technique depends crucially on detection effects, especially the vertex reconstruction resolutions. Our work therefore motivates developments of better reconstruction algorithms and techniques, as well as detector upgrades.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates whether neutron capture positions following Inverse Beta Decay (IBD) in water Cherenkov detectors—particularly with Gd-doped water—can statistically improve neutrino direction reconstruction, despite neutron diffusion; Geant4 simulations show directional correlation persists across 10 MeV–hundreds of MeV, but practical use hinges on vertex resolution improvements.
AI.motivation: IBD events in water Cherenkov detectors (e.g., Super-Kamiokande) lack directional information at low energies due to isotropic positron emission; adding Gadolinium improves neutron capture efficiency and timing/position tagging, raising the question of whether neutron capture location—despite diffusion—retains statistical correlation with initial neutrino direction.
AI.method: Geant4-based Monte Carlo simulation of neutron propagation and capture in water, modeling diffusion and spatial correlation between IBD interaction vertex (neutrino origin) and final neutron capture point across neutrino energies (10 MeV to several hundred MeV); statistical angular reconstruction performance is compared against positron-only inference.
AI.result: Neutron capture position exhibits statistically significant angular correlation with the incident neutrino direction across the studied energy range—even after accounting for neutron diffusion—enabling improved ensemble-level directionality over positron-only methods; however, reconstruction gain degrades rapidly with increasing vertex resolution uncertainty.
AI.conclusion: Neutron capture information in Gd-doped water Cherenkov detectors provides a viable, complementary handle for neutrino direction reconstruction in IBD events, but realizing its potential requires sub-centimeter vertex resolution and improved reconstruction algorithms—motivating detector upgrades and analysis developments.

title: Factorizing quarkonium LDMEs and TMDSTFs using effective field theory
comment: Proceedings for the 33rd International Workshop on Deep Inelastic Scattering and Related Subjects (DIS2026). 7 pages, 3 figures
summary: We use effective field theory to factorize production matrix elements that appear in the NRQCD framework for quarkonium cross sections. By applying a Hubbard-Stratonovich transformation and appropriate field redefinitions, we show that the soft and ultrasoft sectors of NRQCD can be decoupled from the heavy quark and antiquark fields in a hybrid vNRQCD/pNRQCD Lagrangian at leading order in the velocity power-counting. This enables us to re-factorize quarkonium production matrix elements in terms of matrix elements of color-singlet composite fields, which we can write as the wave-function at the origin, and state independent vacuum correlators of chromo-electric and chromo-magnetic gluon fields. This approach verifies powerful relationships between the LDMEs of different S-wave quarkonia originally derived using pNRQCD. Additionally, it allows us to derive new relationships for the production matrix elements used in the transverse momentum dependent factorization (TMD) framework, known as TMD soft transition functions, providing a much stronger set of constraints on these nonperturbative operators. This work significantly advances our understanding of quarkonium production, particularly in the TMD framework.

AI.tldr: This paper uses effective field theory and Hubbard-Stratonovich transformation to decouple soft/ultrasoft sectors from heavy quark fields in a hybrid vNRQCD/pNRQCD Lagrangian, enabling re-factorization of quarkonium production matrix elements into color-singlet wavefunctions and state-independent gluon vacuum correlators; it verifies known LDME relations for S-wave quarkonia and derives new constraints for TMD soft transition functions.
AI.motivation: To improve the theoretical understanding and factorization of quarkonium production matrix elements—especially within the transverse momentum dependent (TMD) framework—by systematically separating scale-dependent dynamics in NRQCD-based effective theories.
AI.method: Effective field theory factorization; Hubbard-Stratonovich transformation; field redefinitions; hybrid vNRQCD/pNRQCD Lagrangian construction; velocity power-counting at leading order.
AI.result: Re-factorized quarkonium production matrix elements expressed as wavefunction at origin times state-independent chromo-electric/magnetic vacuum correlators; verification of existing LDME relations for S-wave quarkonia; derivation of novel constraints on TMD soft transition functions.
AI.conclusion: The decoupling procedure provides a more rigorous and predictive framework for quarkonium production, substantially strengthening nonperturbative constraints—particularly in the TMD formalism—thereby enhancing phenomenological reliability and theoretical consistency.

title: The KSVZ Atlas: A Unified SMEFT-ALP Framework
summary: We develop a general framework for matching KSVZ-like ultraviolet completions featuring vector-like fermions and a spontaneously broken $\mathrm{U}(1)_{\mathrm{PQ}}$ symmetry onto the Standard Model Effective Field Theory and the low-energy axion-like particle effective theory. The framework applies to arbitrary vector-like fermion representations and PQ-charge assignments, and systematically captures the effective interactions generated in both sectors. We then perform a comprehensive phenomenological analysis of the resulting SMEFT operators, based on global fits to electroweak precision, Higgs, and flavor observables, obtaining robust bounds on the corresponding Wilson coefficients that are largely independent of the details of the ultraviolet realization. These constraints can subsequently be translated into the QCD axion and ALP parameter space, providing indirect probes of ALP couplings. We further investigate several representative examples of the interplay between the SMEFT and ALP sectors, illustrating how direct ALP searches and indirect precision and flavor observables provide complementary information on the same underlying dynamics. We find that, over large regions of parameter space, indirect constraints derived from the SMEFT analysis dominate over direct ALP probes, except in scenarios where the PQ-charge assignment permits mass mixing with Standard Model fermions. Overall, our results establish a unified framework for connecting ultraviolet completions, SMEFT analyses, and ALP searches, enabling both the interpretation of existing constraints and the exploration of future signals within a common theoretical setting.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a unified framework linking UV completions of axion-like particles (ALPs) with the Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT) and low-energy ALP effective theory, enabling systematic translation of indirect SMEFT constraints into ALP parameter space and demonstrating their dominance over direct ALP searches in most scenarios.
AI.motivation: To bridge the gap between ultraviolet (UV) completions of axion-like particles—particularly KSVZ-type models with vector-like fermions and spontaneous U(1)_PQ breaking—and low-energy phenomenology, by systematically connecting SMEFT operators and ALP effective couplings for robust, model-independent constraints.
AI.method: Develops a general matching procedure from arbitrary vector-like fermion representations and PQ-charge assignments onto SMEFT and ALP effective theories; performs global fits to electroweak precision, Higgs, and flavor data to constrain SMEFT Wilson coefficients; translates bounds into ALP parameter space; analyzes representative models to compare indirect (SMEFT-based) vs. direct ALP search sensitivities.
AI.result: Obtains robust, UV-model-independent bounds on SMEFT operators; shows indirect constraints dominate direct ALP probes across large regions of parameter space, except when PQ-charge assignments allow ALP–SM fermion mass mixing; identifies complementary information from precision/flavor observables and direct ALP searches.
AI.conclusion: Establishes a unified theoretical framework that consistently connects UV axion completions, SMEFT analyses, and ALP phenomenology—enabling coherent interpretation of current limits and forecasting sensitivity of future experiments.

title: $\boldsymbol{χ_{c1}}(3872)$ and its Partners in the Diabatic Born-Oppenheimer Approximation for QCD
summary: In the Born-Oppenheimer approximation for QCD, the exotic hidden-charm tetraquark meson $χ_{c1}(3872)$ is a near-threshold bound state in Born-Oppenheimer potentials associated with an isospin-0 adjoint meson. The $χ_{c1}(3872)$ is the $1^{++}$ member of a heavy-quark spin-symmetry multiplet whose other members have $J^{PC}$ quantum numbers $0^{++}$, $1^{+-}$, and $2^{++}$. We introduce a simple model for the Born-Oppenheimer potentials that interpolates between the adjoint-meson potential at short distances and the triplet-meson-pair potential at large distances. We take into account the spin splittings of charm mesons nonperturbatively for the first time by solving the diabatic Schrödinger equation. We also take into account the spin splittings of the adjoint meson as well as a narrow avoided crossing with the quarkonium potential. We tune the energy of $χ_{c1}(3872)$ to the $D^* \bar{D}$ threshold and then calculate the spin splittings of the other members of the multiplet and their decay widths into charm-meson pairs. We also calculate the energies and decay widths of the corresponding multiplet of hidden-bottom tetraquarks. These calculations provide a template for the quantitative analysis of all hidden-heavy hadrons using the Born-Oppenheimer approximation for QCD.

AI.tldr: This paper applies the Born-Oppenheimer approximation to QCD to model the exotic tetraquark χ_{c1}(3872) as a near-threshold bound state in adjoint-meson potentials, introduces a diabatic potential model interpolating between short- and long-distance regimes, incorporates charm/bottom meson spin splittings nonperturbatively via the diabatic Schrödinger equation, and predicts masses and decay widths for the full heavy-quark spin-symmetry multiplet — both for hidden-charm and hidden-bottom systems — establishing a quantitative framework for hidden-heavy hadrons.
AI.motivation: To provide a quantitative, first-principles–inspired framework for exotic hidden-heavy tetraquarks (e.g., χ_{c1}(3872)) within QCD using the Born-Oppenheimer approximation, addressing limitations of prior models by nonperturbatively incorporating heavy-meson spin splittings and coupled-channel effects (e.g., avoided crossings with quarkonium).
AI.method: Constructs an interpolated Born-Oppenheimer potential combining adjoint-meson (short-distance) and triplet-meson-pair (long-distance) limits; solves the diabatic Schrödinger equation including nonperturbative spin-dependent couplings for charm and bottom mesons, adjoint-meson spin structure, and a narrow avoided crossing with the quarkonium potential; tunes χ_{c1}(3872) energy to the D* D̄ threshold; computes spin splittings, binding energies, and partial decay widths into charm/bottom meson pairs for the full J^PC multiplet.
AI.result: Predicts masses and decay widths for the full 0^{++}, 1^{++}, 1^{+-}, 2^{++} heavy-quark spin-symmetry multiplet in both hidden-charm and hidden-bottom sectors; reproduces χ_{c1}(3872) as a near-threshold bound state; quantifies impact of spin splittings and avoided crossings; provides benchmark predictions testable in experiment (e.g., LHCb, Belle II).
AI.conclusion: The Born-Oppenheimer approximation, augmented with diabatic coupling and nonperturbative spin treatment, yields a predictive and systematic framework for hidden-heavy tetraquarks; the χ_{c1}(3872) emerges naturally as the 1^{++} member of a spin-symmetry multiplet, and the methodology generalizes to all hidden-heavy hadrons.

title: Sensitivity to top-quark couplings in diboson production at lepton colliders
summary: We study the next-to-leading order electroweak corrections to $e^+e^- \rightarrow W^+W^-$ from dimension-six two-fermion top-quark operators in the Standard Model Effective Field Theory. We compute analytical and numerical results for future electron-positron colliders, focusing on the proposed LEP3 and FCC-ee that will operate at centre-of-mass energies below the $t \bar{t}$ production threshold. We compare the indirect sensitivity arising from virtual corrections to $WW$ production to that from $ZH$ production, and to the current constraints from LEP and LHC data. We show that NLO corrections can provide competitive sensitivity to these operators. This work represents a first step towards the systematic computation of electroweak corrections to $W$-pair production at lepton colliders in the SMEFT, whose impact can then be properly assessed in global analyses.

AI.tldr: This paper computes next-to-leading order (NLO) electroweak corrections to e⁺e⁻ → W⁺W⁻ from dimension-six two-fermion top-quark operators in SMEFT, targeting future lepton colliders (LEP3, FCC-ee) below the tt̄ threshold; it demonstrates competitive indirect sensitivity compared to ZH production and existing LEP/LHC constraints, laying groundwork for systematic SMEFT EW corrections in global fits.
AI.motivation: To assess the indirect sensitivity of future high-luminosity e⁺e⁻ colliders (LEP3, FCC-ee) to SMEFT dimension-six two-fermion top-quark operators via virtual electroweak corrections to W-pair production — especially below the tt̄ threshold where direct top production is kinematically forbidden.
AI.method: Analytical and numerical computation of NLO electroweak corrections to e⁺e⁻ → W⁺W⁻ induced by dimension-six two-fermion top-quark operators in the SMEFT framework; comparison with NLO corrections to e⁺e⁻ → ZH and with current experimental bounds from LEP and LHC.
AI.result: NLO electroweak corrections to W-pair production provide competitive indirect sensitivity to the considered SMEFT operators — comparable to or exceeding that from ZH production and existing collider constraints — particularly at √s ≈ 160–240 GeV (LEP3/FCC-ee energies below tt̄ threshold).
AI.conclusion: NLO electroweak corrections to e⁺e⁻ → W⁺W⁻ constitute a valuable and previously underexploited probe of top-quark-related SMEFT operators; this work establishes the first systematic treatment of such corrections in SMEFT for W-pair production, enabling their inclusion in future global SMEFT analyses.

title: The Fundaments of Unity: ${\mathcal O}(1)$ Couplings in Quantum Field Theories
summary: We critically examine the expectation that in a fundamental quantum field theory, dimensionless couplings in the Lagrangian density should all be of order unity. We propose a measure to quantify the adherence of a theory to this: the spread (the ratio of the largest to the smallest of the magnitudes) of such dimensionless couplings, obtaining various closed-form results. If we take independent identically distributed (IID) couplings to parameterise our uncertainty on the values of the order unity couplings, ratios of couplings can be much larger than one might naively expect. For a theory with 20 IID unit normal couplings, the probability that the magnitude of the ratio of two of them is greater than 100 is 0.29, for example. Even when the IID couplings have exponentially suppressed tails, the distribution of ratios of order one couplings has fat power-law tails which grow with the number of independent couplings.

AI.tldr: The paper challenges the assumption that dimensionless couplings in quantum field theories should be O(1), introducing 'spread' (max/min ratio) as a quantitative measure; it shows that even with O(1) couplings drawn from IID distributions, large coupling ratios arise with non-negligible probability—especially due to fat-tailed distributions of ratios—even for light-tailed parent distributions.
AI.motivation: To critically assess the common expectation that dimensionless Lagrangian couplings in fundamental quantum field theories must be of order unity, and to quantify how 'natural' or 'fine-tuned' a theory is based on coupling spread.
AI.method: Introduces 'spread'—the ratio of largest to smallest magnitude among dimensionless couplings—as a naturalness measure; analytically derives distributions of coupling ratios under independent identically distributed (IID) assumptions—including Gaussian and exponentially tailed distributions—and computes tail probabilities.
AI.result: For 20 IID unit-normal couplings, P(|g_i/g_j| > 100) ≈ 0.29; more generally, ratios of O(1) couplings exhibit fat power-law tails whose exponent weakens with increasing number of couplings—even for light-tailed parent distributions—implying large spreads are statistically typical, not fine-tuned.
AI.conclusion: The 'order-unity' expectation does not guarantee small coupling spreads; large ratios emerge generically from statistical independence, undermining spread-based naturalness arguments unless correlations or physical constraints among couplings are imposed.

title: Collective neutrino oscillations: Many-body non-forward effects and non-classicality
summary: Neutrino evolution in dense astrophysical environments is typically described either within a quantum kinetic framework, which neglects the build-up of multi-body correlations, or through simplified many-body calculations that allow significant entanglement to develop. In this work, we compare these two approaches in a simple neutrino-gas configuration, with particular emphasis on the role of non-forward scattering processes. These effects are incorporated either through a collision term in the kinetic description, or by considering the full neutrino-neutrino many-body Hamiltonian. We highlight differences between the two descriptions in both their characteristic timescales and asymptotic behavior. Motivated by the natural suitability of quantum computing for many-body calculations, we further investigate the non-classicality of neutrino evolution, discussing Trotter error scaling, along with the associated costs of constructing quantum circuits in terms of entangling gates and non-Clifford gates. We find that the resources needed for neutrino many-body evolution are on the low end of typical high-energy physics problems and on the mid to high end with respect to quantum chemistry problems. For the full Hamiltonian, resource requirements increase relative to the truncated version. We emphasize the importance of efficient fermion-to-qubit encodings, which are essential for reducing the substantial computational resources required for such simulations.

AI.tldr: This paper compares quantum kinetic and many-body approaches for modeling neutrino evolution in dense astrophysical environments, focusing on non-forward scattering; it quantifies quantum resource requirements for simulating the full vs. truncated neutrino-neutrino Hamiltonian, highlighting the critical role of fermion-to-qubit encodings.
AI.motivation: To reconcile discrepancies between quantum kinetic (mean-field) and many-body descriptions of neutrino evolution—particularly regarding non-forward scattering—and to assess feasibility and resource demands of quantum simulation for neutrino many-body dynamics.
AI.method: Analytical and numerical comparison of quantum kinetic equations (with collision terms) versus exact many-body treatment using the full neutrino-neutrino Hamiltonian in a simplified neutrino-gas setup; quantum resource analysis includes Trotter error scaling, entangling gate counts, and non-Clifford gate costs under various fermion-to-qubit mappings (e.g., Jordan-Wigner, Bravyi-Kitaev).
AI.result: Significant differences in timescales and asymptotic behavior between kinetic and many-body descriptions; quantum simulation of full Hamiltonian demands more resources than truncated version; required resources are modest relative to high-energy physics but substantial compared to typical quantum chemistry problems; optimal fermion-to-qubit encoding drastically reduces qubit and gate overhead.
AI.conclusion: Quantum many-body methods capture essential physics beyond kinetic theory—especially non-forward correlations—but require careful resource-aware implementation; efficient encodings and error-controlled Trotterization are indispensable for viable near-term quantum simulation of neutrino evolution.

title: When direct detection constrains reheating temperature: freeze-in with stronger couplings and inflaton-seeded freeze-in
summary: Recent results from the DAMIC-M and PandaX collaborations have excluded the standard freeze-in production of dark matter for masses in the range $3~\mathrm{MeV} \lesssim m_χ\lesssim 1~\mathrm{GeV}$ in the context of extensions of the Standard Model featuring an additional ultra-light $U(1)_{\rm X}$ gauge boson. In this work, we analyze the constraints induced by DAMIC-M and PandaX results on the reheating temperature in freeze-in models at stronger coupling, or when a non-thermal source (such as inflaton decay) comes into play. We identify viable scenarios in which the DM relic abundance is correctly reproduced while evading current experimental bounds on the electron-scattering cross section, $\overlineσ_\mathrm{e}$. In particular, we show that for reheating temperatures below the electroweak scale, Boltzmann suppressed production can be compensated by stronger couplings, bringing freeze-in scenarios within present experimental reach. Finally, we study a hybrid scenario in which a small branching ratio of inflaton decay seeds a nonzero initial dark-matter abundance. We show that such contributions can significantly modify freeze-in predictions across broad regions of parameter space, offering an additional pathway for probing extremely feeble interactions.

AI.tldr: This paper re-examines freeze-in dark matter production in the presence of an ultra-light U(1)_X gauge boson, using DAMIC-M and PandaX constraints on electron-scattering cross sections. It explores how lower reheating temperatures and non-thermal inflaton decay can reconcile viable DM abundance with current experimental limits.
AI.motivation: To reassess freeze-in dark matter scenarios in light of recent direct detection constraints (DAMIC-M, PandaX) that exclude standard freeze-in for 3 MeV ≲ m_χ ≲ 1 GeV, and to identify viable alternatives—such as sub-electroweak reheating or inflaton-driven non-thermal production—that evade these bounds while reproducing the observed relic density.
AI.method: Analytical and numerical computation of dark matter production rates, including thermal freeze-in (with variable reheating temperature T_R), Boltzmann-suppressed contributions at low T_R, and hybrid non-thermal production via inflaton decay; comparison with electron-recoil limits from DAMIC-M and PandaX to constrain the effective electron-scattering cross section σ̄_e.
AI.result: Identifies viable parameter space where freeze-in remains consistent with data: (i) T_R < T_EW enables stronger couplings without overproducing DM due to Boltzmann suppression; (ii) a small inflaton branching ratio to DM can seed initial abundance, altering total yield and relaxing σ̄_e constraints across broad coupling/mass regions.
AI.conclusion: Standard freeze-in is excluded in the 3 MeV–1 GeV window under typical assumptions, but non-standard cosmological histories—low reheating or hybrid inflaton seeding—restore viability and extend experimental sensitivity to otherwise inaccessible feeble interactions.
